content.content:
Quick checks:

```bash
./build.sh          # assemble hlasm.s (sanity check)
./demo.sh           # show a demo source, hlasm's output, and that it assembles
./build.sh test     # run the regression suite
```

## Running hlasm

hlasm reads its source from memory at address 0x080000 (524288), so a run has
three parts: turn the source into a loadable image, run hlasm on the emulator
with that image loaded, and keep the UART output.

```bash
# 1. Source text -> loadable image
bash demos/make_bin.sh prog.hlasm prog.bin

# 2. Run hlasm with the image at 0x080000; -q prints only the UART output
scripts/run-kernel.sh hlasm.s --load-binary prog.bin@524288 \
    --speed 0 -n 5000000 -q 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^Executed' > prog.s

# 3. Assemble and run the generated program
scripts/run-kernel.sh prog.s --speed 0 -n 100000
```

Notes:

- `-n` is the instruction budget for the emulator. hlasm costs roughly 10-15
  thousand instructions per source line (it makes two passes); give it
  plenty, it stops by itself when done. `--speed 0` runs at full speed.
- hlasm ends by spinning on `bra` to itself (how COR24 halts); `cor24-emu`
  detects this and stops.
- If hlasm stops with a line starting `ERROR:`, the source exceeded a limit
  or contains an error (see [Limits and error messages](#limits-and-error-messages)).
- The main source can be up to 32,767 bytes this way. Larger programs, or
  programs split into several files, use a source set
  ([INCLUDE and COPY](#multiple-source-files-include-and-copy)).

## Source format

- One statement per line, at most 256 characters.
- Lines starting with `;` are comments and are copied to the output.
- `name:` at the start of a line defines a label (passed to `cor24-asm`).
- Instructions are written as in COR24 assembly, conventionally indented by
  one space: ` add r0,1`.
- hlasm directives (`MACRO`, `SET`, `IF`, `DO`, ...) start in column 1 or
  after blanks and are upper case.
- Anything hlasm does not recognize is passed through unchanged, so any
  valid COR24 assembly is also valid hlasm source.

## Named constants: EQU and SET

```
name EQU expression
SET name,expression
```

## Project Structure

```
hlasm.s        -- COR24 assembly source (the macro-assembler)
bootstrap/     -- reduced self-hosting subset sources and proof points
build.sh       -- build / test / run script
scripts/       -- run-kernel.sh: assemble hlasm.s (cor24-asm) and run it (cor24-emu)
demo.sh        -- demo script
justfile       -- just targets
docs/          -- architecture, prd, design, plan
reg-rs/        -- reg-rs test specifications and baselines
```

## Documentation

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) -- system overview and memory layout
- [Bootstrap Plan](docs/bootstrap.md) -- staged self-hosting path and blockers
- [PRD](docs/prd.md) -- product requirements and scope
- [Design](docs/design.md) -- syntax, lowering rules, data structures
- [Plan](docs/plan.md) -- step-by-step implementation roadmap

## Related Repositories

- [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator) -- COR24 emulator (`cor24-emu`)
- [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler) -- COR24 cross-assembler (`cor24-asm`)
- [sw-cor24-forth](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-forth) -- Forth for COR24
- [sw-cor24-rpg-ii](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-rpg-ii) -- RPG-II for COR24
- [sw-cor24-project](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project) -- ecosystem hub

## Running hlasm

The quickest way to run a program is `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh`. It runs hlasm,
assembles the result with `cor24-asm`, runs that on `cor24-emu`, and prints
only the program's UART output:

```bash
scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh prog.hlasm              # a single source file
scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh prog.sourceset          # MAIN plus INCLUDE/COPY members
scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh --keep-s prog.s prog.hlasm -- -u 'input\n'
```

`--keep-s` also saves the generated assembly, `--hlasm-n` and `--run-n` set
the two instruction budgets (10,000,000 and 1,000,000 by default), and
arguments after `--` go to the program's `cor24-emu`. It exits 2 when hlasm
reports an `ERROR:` or runs out of budget, 3 when `cor24-asm` rejects the
output, and 4 when the program does not halt within its budget, with the
reason on stderr.

The rest of this section shows the stages by hand. hlasm reads

# Architecture

## Overview

sw-cor24-hlasm is a **macro-assembler** for the COR24 24-bit RISC ISA,
written entirely in COR24 assembly. It reads HLASM-inspired structured
assembly source from an in-memory text buffer and emits plain COR24
assembly (`.s` output via UART).

The macro-assembler runs on the COR24 emulator (`cor24-emu`) just like
sw-cor24-forth and sw-cor24-rpg-ii.

**Product statement**: A COR24 macro-assembler, written in COR24 assembly,
that processes HLASM-inspired source and produces plain COR24 assembly output.

## Processing Pipeline

```
.hlasm source (loaded into memory)
     |
     v
+-------------------------------+
| HLASM Macro-Assembler         |
|  (COR24 assembly program)     |
|   Scanner / tokenizer         |
|   Macro table lookup          |
|   Macro expansion             |
|   Conditional assembly eval   |
|   Structured lowering         |
|   Symbol table management     |
+-------------------------------+
     |
     v
UART output: plain .s assembly
     |
     v
cor24-asm out.s -o out.lgo; cor24-emu --lgo out.lgo
```

The macro-assembler is a COR24 program that reads text and writes text.
It is not a host-side tool -- it runs on the target.

## Platform

COR24 24-bit RISC: 3 GP registers (r0-r2), fp, sp, z, iv, ir,
24-bit words, variable-length instructions (1/2/4 bytes), UART at 0xFF0100.

## Memory Layout

| Region | Address | Contents |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Code + immutable tables | 0x000000+ | HLASM macro-assembler assembly (must end below 0x010000) |
| Assembler tables | 0x010000-0x03FFFF | Symbol table (512), macro table (256), 64 KB macro body pool, work area (line/name/operand buffers, 32-deep stacks), XREF/HLDIAG tables, macro expansion frames (8), source descriptors (33) |
| Source config block | 0x07F000 | Member count, main overrides and name, up to 32 member records (base, length, 15-char name), loaded by `--load-binary` (built by `reg-rs/make_cfg.sh`) |
| Source/include buffers | 0x080000-0x0BFFFF | Preloaded ASCII HLASM input buffers |
| Runtime arena | 0x0C0000-0x0C125B | Counters, current source slot, source-return stack (16) |
| Relaxation state | 0x0D0000-0x0ECFFF | Two-pass structured-jump snapshot and tables |
| Stack | 0xFEEC00 | Preferred 3K EBR stack (`--stack-kilobytes 3`) |

Every table has a capacity check that stops with `ERROR: ...` instead of
overflowing; the limits and the exact layout are in
`docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md`. Loaded source text and assembler-owned
mutable state stay in separate SRAM regions.

Named library members use the same low-SRAM table as named includes. `COPY name`
is treated as an explicit HLASM-style alias for that path, so macro and symbol
libraries can be packaged as source-set members without adding a second runtime
resolver.

An opt-in listing layer also exists at source level: `SET HLIST,1` causes the
runtime to emit semicolon comment records for copied members, macro definition
sites, macro expansion sites, and selected consumed directives. This is kept
separate from `SET HLANN,1`, which only annotates structured control-flow
lowering.

A second opt-in visibility layer exists for end-of-run reporting: `SET HLXREF,1`
causes the runtime to emit a compact xref section for copied members, macro
definitions, macro expansion counts, and assembly-time symbols observed through
`SET`/`EQU`.

A third opt-in layer is the diagnostic channel: `SET HLDIAG,1` activates a
central warn routine that emits `; !! hlasm: <msg> at src<id>:<line>` lines
into the generated stream when callers invoke it. The read path maintains a
per-source line counter and a monotonic source-id counter, so any future
diagnostic can locate itself relative to the input. The first real caller
runs at the pass-through path: if the line's mnemonic-position token is not
a known COR24 mnemonic (checked against the existing `_mn_table`), a macro,
a hlasm-owned directive, a label, a comment, or a `.`-prefixed raw directive,
hlasm emits an `unknown mnemonic '<token>'` warning and still passes the
original line through unchanged. A second real caller is piggybacked on the
HLXREF rails: whenever `_eval_expr_ptr` looks up a `SET`/`EQU` term that
isn't in the symbol table, the name is recorded in a small undef-names set
(capped at 16) and an `undefined symbol '<name>'` warning is emitted once
per distinct name as part of the end-of-run pass.

## Components

### Scanner
Reads input text character by character. Identifies keywords (MACRO, MEND,
IF, DO, SELECT, etc.), mnemonics, register names, numbers, labels, comments.
Produces a token stream in memory.

### Macro Table
Stores macro definitions: name, parameter list, body token stream.
Lookup on macro invocation. Supports nested macros.

Current compatibility baseline is intentionally narrower than full IBM HLASM:
simple `MACRO ... MEND` definitions are consumed rather than emitted, simple
invocation-by-name expansion is stable, positional `&1`/`&2` substitution
works, and HLASM-style named `&arg` substitution works. Full local-label
compatibility and broader macro robustness are still being hardened in later
steps.
Macro names up to 31 characters are supported, and repeated `\@` local-label
expansion now stays distinct across multiple macro definitions and invocations.
Macro bodies still expand directly to emitted plain-text lines; the assembler
does not yet reparse conditional-assembly or structured-control-flow
directives that appear inside macro bodies.

### Macro Expander
Substitutes positional `&N` and named `&name` parameters, with named
parameters rewritten onto the positional expansion path at record time.
Generates unique local labels (`\@` -> unique counter). Handles nested
expansion with depth limit.

### Conditional Assembly
Evaluates SET symbols, IFDEF, IFEQ at assembly time. Includes or excludes
source sections based on conditions.

### Structured Lowering
Transforms IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF, DO/ENDDO, SELECT/WHEN/ENDSEL into plain
labels and branches. Generates unique branch target labels. Because raw COR24
branches only have an 8-bit PC-relative reach, structured lowering uses
long-range-safe forms for generated control flow: reversed short conditional
branches skip over unconditional `jmp` instructions, and generated
unconditional structured transfers emit `jmp` directly instead of `bra`.

### Symbol Table
Tracks small assembly-time symbols for `SET` and `EQU`. These values are used
during conditional assembly and structured-lowering constant handling.
Ordinary assembler label arithmetic remains passthrough to the downstream
assembler rather than being evaluated inside `hlasm`.

### Output Emitter
Writes expanded, lowered assembly text to the output buffer. Flushes to UART.

## Register Allocation

External code generation still follows the Forth/RPG-II style register roles,
but internal `hlasm.s` helper routines now use a stricter calling convention
for correctness and predictability.

| Register | Use |
|----------|-----|
| r0 | Return value / caller-saved scratch |
| r1 | Return address from `jal`, volatile scratch |
| r2 | Callee-saved working register |
| fp | Frame pointer for subroutines |
| sp | Data stack (hardware push/pop) |

Internal helper ABI rules:

- A helper that writes `r2` must save and restore it before returning.
- Callers must assume `r0` and `r1` are clobbered by any helper call.
- `fp` and `sp` must always be restored by the callee.
- This convention is defensive rather than minimal: helper composition should
  stay correct even as implementations change internally.

## I/O Model

- **Input**: .hlasm source loaded into memory via `--load-binary`
- **Output**: plain .s assembly emitted via UART
- **UART**: character I/O at 0xFF0100

## Dependency Relationship

```
sw-cor24-hlasm (this project)
  |
  |  runs on
  v
sw-cor24-emulator (cor24-emu), after sw-cor24-x-assembler (cor24-asm)
  assembles hlasm.s to .lgo -- scripts/run-kernel.sh joins the two
```

## Testing Strategy

Tests use **reg-rs** (golden-output regression testing), following the same
pattern as sw-cor24-forth and sw-cor24-rpg-ii:

1. Each test is a `.rgt` file with a `scripts/run-kernel.sh hlasm.s` command
2. Input source loaded via `--load-binary`
3. Preprocess filter extracts UART output
4. Tests run via `reg-rs run -p hlasm --parallel`

## COR24 ISA Constraints

- 24-bit words (3 bytes), little-endian
- 3 GPRs (r0, r1, r2), plus fp, sp, z, iv, ir
- Single condition flag C (set by ceq/cls/clu)
- Variable-length instructions: 1, 2, or 4 bytes (never 3)
- Branches: signed 8-bit PC-relative offset (-128..+127), +4 pipeline bias
- Load destinations limited to r0, r1, r2 only (not fp, sp)
- ALU destinations limited to r0, r1, r2 only
- No mov r0,sp -- must use mov fp,sp; push fp; pop r0
- 16 MB address space: 1 MB SRAM + 8 KB EBR + I/O

## Build / Test

```bash
just build        # assemble check
just test         # run reg-rs regression suite
just demo         # run example
./build.sh        # build script
./demo.sh         # demo script
./demo.sh test    # test suite
```

All shell scripts for build/test. No Python/Rust/C in the project.
Follows sw-cor24-forth and sw-cor24-rpg-ii patterns.

## Non-Goals

- No types, type system, or record system
- No general-purpose compile-time programming language
- No optimizing transformations
- No relocatable object format or linker
- No runtime abstractions hidden behind macros
- No expression semantics approaching C/PL/I/PL/SW

**On your question:** the C demos are not ported yet. Porting them is steps 11–13, so working C demos are about six more steps away. HLASM itself is usable now, and with this step it's at a good stopping point:

- macros that call macros, with default and keyword parameters;
- structured IF/DO/SELECT jumps at any distance;
- EQU and expressions;
- source sets of up to 32 named files, with errors that name the file and line;
- a one-command way to run a program and see its output.

The demos that print output (d40, d41, d42) assemble and run correctly on cor24-emu. Everything the HLASM self-hosting plan needed is also in place.

**Step 8 is done.** All 77 regression tests pass, and it's committed and pushed to `feat/tinyc-macro-ports`.

- **New script, `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh`:** you give it a `.hlasm` file or a source set. It runs hlasm, assembles the result with cor24-asm, runs that on cor24-emu, and prints only the program's output.
  - If a stage fails it stops and exits with a code naming the stage: 2 for an hlasm error, 3 if cor24-asm rejects the output, 4 if the program never halts.
  - `--keep-s` saves the generated assembly. `--hlasm-n` and `--run-n` set the instruction limits. Anything after `--` goes to the program's emulator, for example UART input.
  - The emulator exits 0 even when it hits its instruction limit. So the script compares the reported instruction count with the limit to tell a program that halted from one that was cut off.
- **New test convention, `hlasm_e2e_*`:** these tests record what the program prints rather than hlasm's generated text. They keep passing when the generated code changes but the program behaves the same.
  - `hlasm_e2e_d40_long_range` replaces the old demo 40 run test.
  - `hlasm_e2e_harness` covers a source set that pulls in a macro library with COPY (it prints "COPY ok") and checks all three failure exit codes.
  - The demo 41 and 42 run tests still use the old form. I left them alone to keep this step's scope to one conversion; switching them over is trivial.
- **Docs:** the user guide's "Running hlasm" section now starts with the script. The README and architecture doc mention it too.

**Next:** step 9 surveys the tiny-C demos and catalogs the macros they need. I'll start it when you say go.

=== PLAN ===

content.content:
# Migrating the PL/SW Compiler from C to HLASM

Status: plan (2026-10-30). No migration work has started.

## Goal

Today the PL/SW compiler is written in C (`src/*.h`, `src/main.c`) and
built by tc24r, a host-side cross-compiler. The long-term goal is a
PL/SW compiler written in PL/SW. This plan covers the intermediate
step: porting the compiler from C to HLASM source assembled by
[sw-cor24-hlasm](../../sw-cor24-hlasm), which runs on COR24 itself.

The resulting bootstrap chain needs no host compiler:

```
hlasm.s (hand-written COR24 asm)
   -> assembles plsw-in-HLASM          (this plan, phases 1-4)
      -> compiles plsw-in-PL/SW        (phase 5, separate saga)
         -> compiles itself (fixpoint)
```

Why go through HLASM instead of porting C straight to PL/SW:

- It removes tc24r from the trust and bootstrap chain. Every stage
  after `hlasm.s` is built on COR24.
- The C-to-HLASM port is mechanical. Each C function maps to one HLASM
  routine that follows tc24r's calling convention, so the result can
  be checked against tc24r's output one function at a time.
- sw-cor24-hlasm's active `tinyc-macro-ports` saga is already proving
  exactly this porting pattern on the tiny-C demos. This plan reuses
  that work rather than inventing a new method.

## Precursor: sw-cor24-hlasm `tinyc-macro-ports`

That saga ports `../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos` from C to HLASM. Its
steps, and what each one gives this plan:

| hlasm step | Delivers | Needed here for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 structured-jmp-relaxation | `IF`/`DO`/`SELECT` output that `cor24-asm` accepts at any branch distance | Large routines (codegen has 45 functions in 1,747 lines of C) |
| 2 e2e-run-harness | `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh` (hlasm -> .s -> asm -> run) | The build and test loop |
| 3 tinyc-survey-and-macro-catalog | `docs/tinyc-port-plan.md`: idiom catalog and macro gaps | The C-idiom-to-macro mapping |
| 4 macro-library-core | `lib/` COPY members: PROLOG/EPILOG/CALL/RET, UART, data | Shared library for every compiler module |
| 5-7 port demos | Proof on I/O, control flow, functions, arrays, structs, strings | Confidence that every construct in `src/` has a port pattern |
| 8 macro-value-showcase | C vs tc24r `.s` vs HLASM side by side | Size and readability baseline |

Phase 0 of this plan waits for steps 1-4 at minimum. Steps 5-7 should
land before phase 2 starts.

## Source Layout: Single Translation Unit, Like Today

The C compiler has no libraries and no separate compilation. `main.c`
includes every module header, the headers hold all function bodies,
and tc24r emits a single `plsw.s`. The HLASM version keeps the same
shape:

```
hlasm/
  plsw.hlasm          main member: COPY each module in dependency order
  str.hlasm           one member per C header, same names
  arena.hlasm
  chunk.hlasm
  io.hlasm
  token.hlasm
  lexer.hlasm
  ast.hlasm
  symtab.hlasm
  types.hlasm
  layout.hlasm
  emit.hlasm
  parser.hlasm
  macro.hlasm
  codegen.hlasm
  compile.hlasm
  plsw.sourceset      source set naming the main member and all COPY members
lib/                  vendored macro library from sw-cor24-hlasm
```

hlasm already supports this through `COPY`/`INCLUDE` named members and
`.sourceset` manifests (`SOURCESET`, `PROFILE`, packed extra buffers).
One hlasm run reads all members and writes one `.s`, so no linker is
needed, which matches the current C build.

Differences from C that the port has to handle:

- **One global label namespace.** C `static` helpers and locals are
  scoped; HLASM labels are not. Prefix every routine and data label
  with its module (`lex_`, `cg_`, ...). tc24r already emits global
  `_name` labels, so keeping the C names is the default.
- **Include guards.** The C headers use `#ifndef X_H` guards. In HLASM,
  either list each member exactly once in `plsw.hlasm`, or use an
  `IFNDEF`/`SET` guard per member. Listing once is simpler and enough.
- **Capacity.** Every member must fit in hlasm's source window at the
  same time, and every routine label, macro and `SET` symbol shares one
  set of tables. See blockers B1-B3 below.

## Phases

Each phase ends with every regression check green (see Verification).

### Phase 0: hlasm readiness

Fix the hlasm blockers listed below, in sw-cor24-hlasm, before any
compiler code is ported. Exit gate: hlasm assembles a synthetic,
compiler-sized source (roughly the expected line, label and macro
counts) split across ~16 COPY members, and `cor24-asm` accepts the
output.

### Phase 1: Freeze and baseline

- Freeze language feature work in the C compiler. Bug fixes still go
  into C and are ported along with everything else.
- Build the golden corpus: the `.s` output of the current C compiler for
  every `reg-rs` test, every `examples/*.plsw`, and the large
  downstream sources (e.g. sw-cor24-snobol4's `sno_engine.plsw`). The
  HLASM compiler must reproduce these byte for byte.
- Record the baseline: `plsw.s` size, `.lgo` size, cycle counts per
  golden, peak stack depth.
- Vendor hlasm (`hlasm.s`, `lib/`, the source-set runner) under
  `vendor/` following [vendor-plan.md](vendor-plan.md).

### Phase 2: Port the runtime modules (leaves)

Port in dependency order, leaves first:

1. `str` (8 functions), `arena` (5), `chunk` (4), `io` (7)
2. `token` (5), `lexer` (32)
3. `ast` (15), `symtab` (11), `types` (21), `layout` (8)

Hybrid build while porting: the build uses tc24r's `plsw.s` with the
ported functions removed, plus hlasm's output for those functions.
This works because the HLASM routines follow tc24r's calling convention
(args on the stack right to left, result in r0, `push fp/r2/r1`
prologue, first arg at `fp+9`) and keep tc24r's `_name` labels. Add a
`scripts/splice-plsw.sh` that drops ported functions from the tc24r
`.s` by label range and appends the HLASM output.

After each module: the golden corpus is byte-identical and the
`test_main.c` unit tests for that module still pass. The unit tests
remain C, built against the hybrid, until phase 4.

### Phase 3: Port the compiler core

4. `emit` (32)
5. `parser` (23)
6. `macro` (27)
7. `codegen` (45). This is the largest module. Split it into several
   COPY members by statement or expression family if routine sizes
   push structured-branch relaxation or table limits.
8. `compile` (5), `main.c` (buffers, UART protocol, mode dispatch)

Large static buffers (`src_buf` 192 KiB, `inc_buf` 32 KiB) become
`.space` reservations, which hlasm passes through to the output.

### Phase 4: Cut over

- `just build` runs hlasm instead of tc24r. Remove tc24r from
  `vendor/active.env` and the justfile.
- Replace `src/test_main.c`. Turn each unit test into a reg-rs test that
  drives the compiler through its UART protocol, or port the harness
  to HLASM. Choose per test.
- Move `src/` to `archive/c-src/` (kept for reference until phase 5
  ends) and update README, CLAUDE.md, `docs/architecture.md`,
  `docs/usage.md`.
- Acceptance: the golden corpus is byte-identical; `.lgo` size and
  cycle counts are within an agreed margin of the C baseline (proposed:
  +10% size, +10% cycles); peak stack fits the EBR stack.

# Migrating the PL/SW Compiler from C to HLASM

Status: plan (2026-10-30). No migration work has started.

## Goal

Today the PL/SW compiler is written in C (`src/*.h`, `src/main.c`) and
built by tc24r, a host-side cross-compiler. The long-term goal is a
PL/SW compiler written in PL/SW. This plan covers the intermediate
step: porting the compiler from C to HLASM source assembled by
[sw-cor24-hlasm](../../sw-cor24-hlasm), which runs on COR24 itself.

The resulting bootstrap chain needs no host compiler:

```
hlasm.s (hand-written COR24 asm)
   -> assembles plsw-in-HLASM          (this plan, phases 1-4)
      -> compiles plsw-in-PL/SW        (phase 5, separate saga)
         -> compiles itself (fixpoint)
```

Why go through HLASM instead of porting C straight to PL/SW:

- It removes tc24r from the trust and bootstrap chain. Every stage
  after `hlasm.s` is built on COR24.
- The C-to-HLASM port is mechanical. Each C function maps to one HLASM
  routine that follows tc24r's calling convention, so the result can
  be checked against tc24r's output one function at a time.
- sw-cor24-hlasm's active `tinyc-macro-ports` saga is already proving
  exactly this porting pattern on the tiny-C demos. This plan reuses
  that work rather than inventing a new method.

## Precursor: sw-cor24-hlasm `tinyc-macro-ports`

That saga ports `../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos` from C to HLASM. Its
steps, and what each one gives this plan:

| hlasm step | Delivers | Needed here for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 structured-jmp-relaxation | `IF`/`DO`/`SELECT` output that `cor24-asm` accepts at any branch distance | Large routines (codegen has 45 functions in 1,747 lines of C) |
| 2 e2e-run-harness | `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh` (hlasm -> .s -> asm -> run) | The build and test loop |
| 3 tinyc-survey-and-macro-catalog | `docs/tinyc-port-plan.md`: idiom catalog and macro gaps | The C-idiom-to-macro mapping |
| 4 macro-library-core | `lib/` COPY members: PROLOG/EPILOG/CALL/RET, UART, data | Shared library for every compiler module |
| 5-7 port demos | Proof on I/O, control flow, functions, arrays, structs, strings | Confidence that every construct in `src/` has a port pattern |
| 8 macro-value-showcase | C vs tc24r `.s` vs HLASM side by side | Size and readability baseline |

Phase 0 of this plan waits for steps 1-4 at minimum. Steps 5-7 should
land before phase 2 starts.

## Source Layout: Single Translation Unit, Like Today

The C compiler has no libraries and no separate compilation. `main.c`
includes every module header, the headers hold all function bodies,
and tc24r emits a single `plsw.s`. The HLASM version keeps the same
shape:

```
hlasm/
  plsw.hlasm          main member: COPY each module in dependency order
  str.hlasm           one member per C header, same names
  arena.hlasm
  chunk.hlasm
  io.hlasm
  token.hlasm
  lexer.hlasm
  ast.hlasm
  symtab.hlasm
  types.hlasm
  layout.hlasm
  emit.hlasm
  parser.hlasm
  macro.hlasm
  codegen.hlasm
  compile.hlasm
  plsw.sourceset      source set naming the main member and all COPY members
lib/                  vendored macro library from sw-cor24-hlasm
```

hlasm already supports this through `COPY`/`INCLUDE` named members and
`.sourceset` manifests (`SOURCESET`, `PROFILE`, packed extra buffers).
One hlasm run reads all members and writes one `.s`, so no linker is
needed, which matches the current C build.

Differences from C that the port has to handle:

- **One global label namespace.** C `static` helpers and locals are
  scoped; HLASM labels are not. Prefix every routine and data label
  with its module (`lex_`, `cg_`, ...). tc24r already emits global
  `_name` labels, so keeping the C names is the default.
- **Include guards.** The C headers use `#ifndef X_H` guards. In HLASM,
  either list each member exactly once in `plsw.hlasm`, or use an
  `IFNDEF`/`SET` guard per member. Listing once is simpler and enough.
- **Capacity.** Every member must fit in hlasm's source window at the
  same time, and every routine label, macro and `SET` symbol shares one
  set of tables. See blockers B1-B3 below.

## Phases

Each phase ends with every regression check green (see Verification).

### Phase 0: hlasm readiness

Fix the hlasm blockers listed below, in sw-cor24-hlasm, before any
compiler code is ported. Exit gate: hlasm assembles a synthetic,
compiler-sized source (roughly the expected line, label and macro
counts) split across ~16 COPY members, and `cor24-asm` accepts the
output.

### Phase 1: Freeze and baseline

- Freeze language feature work in the C compiler. Bug fixes still go
  into C and are ported along with everything else.
- Build the golden corpus: the `.s` output of the current C compiler for
  every `reg-rs` test, every `examples/*.plsw`, and the large
  downstream sources (e.g. sw-cor24-snobol4's `sno_engine.plsw`). The
  HLASM compiler must reproduce these byte for byte.
- Record the baseline: `plsw.s` size, `.lgo` size, cycle counts per
  golden, peak stack depth.
- Vendor hlasm (`hlasm.s`, `lib/`, the source-set runner) under
  `vendor/` following [vendor-plan.md](vendor-plan.md).

### Phase 2: Port the runtime modules (leaves)

Port in dependency order, leaves first:

1. `str` (8 functions), `arena` (5), `chunk` (4), `io` (7)
2. `token` (5), `lexer` (32)
3. `ast` (15), `symtab` (11), `types` (21), `layout` (8)

Hybrid build while porting: the build uses tc24r's `plsw.s` with the
ported functions removed, plus hlasm's output for those functions.
This works because the HLASM routines follow tc24r's calling convention
(args on the stack right to left, result in r0, `push fp/r2/r1`
prologue, first arg at `fp+9`) and keep tc24r's `_name` labels. Add a
`scripts/splice-plsw.sh` that drops ported functions from the tc24r
`.s` by label range and appends the HLASM output.

After each module: the golden corpus is byte-identical and the
`test_main.c` unit tests for that module still pass. The unit tests
remain C, built against the hybrid, until phase 4.

### Phase 3: Port the compiler core

4. `emit` (32)
5. `parser` (23)
6. `macro` (27)
7. `codegen` (45). This is the largest module. Split it into several
   COPY members by statement or expression family if routine sizes
   push structured-branch relaxation or table limits.
8. `compile` (5), `main.c` (buffers, UART protocol, mode dispatch)

Large static buffers (`src_buf` 192 KiB, `inc_buf` 32 KiB) become
`.space` reservations, which hlasm passes through to the output.

### Phase 4: Cut over

- `just build` runs hlasm instead of tc24r. Remove tc24r from
  `vendor/active.env` and the justfile.
- Replace `src/test_main.c`. Turn each unit test into a reg-rs test that
  drives the compiler through its UART protocol, or port the harness
  to HLASM. Choose per test.
- Move `src/` to `archive/c-src/` (kept for reference until phase 5
  ends) and update README, CLAUDE.md, `docs/architecture.md`,
  `docs/usage.md`.
- Acceptance: the golden corpus is byte-identical; `.lgo` size and
  cycle counts are within an agreed margin of the C baseline (proposed:
  +10% size, +10% cycles); peak stack fits the EBR stack.

### Phase 5: PL/SW self-hosting (separate saga, outline only)

- Use the HLASM-built compiler as stage 1 to compile a PL/SW rewrite
  (stage 2). Stage 2 compiles itself (stage 3). Accept when
  `stage2.s == stage3.s`.
- Language gaps to plan for before starting: deep `ELSE IF` chains
  exhaust the compiler stack (issue #33, so use `SELECT`), and
  separate compilation relies on `link24`, a host-side Rust tool.
- The HLASM compiler stays as the bootstrap seed and is frozen once
  stage 2 is accepted.

| ID | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Structured conditions take a single compare (`cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt`, `cc_lu`, `cc_zset`, `cc_zclr`). There is no `AND`/`OR`, and no `>`/`<=` forms. | C `&&`/`||` must be lowered by hand into nested `IF`s or `DOEXIT` chains. Compound conditions would cut much of that noise. |
| G2 | `SET`/`EQU` expressions allow only `+` and `-`. | Struct field offsets and sizes (`ast`, `symtab`, `layout`) want `*` for array strides at least. |
| G3 | Struct layout helpers (an HLASM `DSECT`-style block or `FIELD name,size` macro that accumulates offsets). | Without this, every node and symbol field offset is a hand-written `EQU`. |
| G4 | String literal emission with escapes (`\n`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"`, `\0`). *verify* what `.ascii`/`.asciz` passthrough handles. | Hundreds of compiler messages and emitted asm fragments are C strings. |
| G5 | The 128-byte line buffer. | Long `.byte` tables and long emitted-asm string data may exceed it. |
| G6 | Diagnostics that point at the original member and line for errors inside `COPY` members. | `HLDIAG` already tracks a source id and line; it needs to cover every error path at this scale. |
| G7 | Assembly time. hlasm is two-pass and runs on the emulator. | Measure cycles for a full compiler build in phase 0, and set a budget so the edit-build-test loop stays usable. |

When a port step hits a gap that is not listed here, stop. Add the
gap to this table and fix it in sw-cor24-hlasm as its own step, rather
than working around it in the port. The hlasm saga follows the same
rule.

## Verification

At every step:

- `just test` (reg-rs): all goldens pass.
- Golden corpus: the compiler's `.s` output is byte-identical to the C
  baseline for every input.
- Unit tests (`test_main.c` against the hybrid build) pass until
  phase 4 replaces them.
- Size and cycle report compared with the phase 1 baseline, flagging
  regressions over the agreed margin.

## Risks

- **Capacity growth in hlasm (B1-B3)** could turn into a redesign, for
  example moving tables to a heap arena. This should be found in
  phase 0, not partway through phase 3.
- **Code size.** Macro-expanded HLASM may be larger than tc24r's output.
  The compiler image plus 224 KiB of buffers has to fit in 1 MB of
  SRAM next to hlasm's own load windows during builds.
- **Stack depth.** The parser and codegen recurse. Hand-written frames
  can be smaller than tc24r's, but deep recursion still has to fit the
  EBR stack (see issue #33).
- **Two codebases during the port.** The C freeze in phase 1 limits
  this; bug fixes have to land in both until phase 4.

One AgentRail step per line, with each module step small enough for
one branch:

4. `golden-corpus-baseline`: phase 1 corpus, size and cycle baseline
5. `vendor-hlasm`: vendor hlasm and `lib/`, add `hlasm/plsw.sourceset`
6. `hybrid-splice-build`: `scripts/splice-plsw.sh` plus a just target
7. `port-str-arena-chunk-io`
8. `port-token-lexer`
9. `port-ast-symtab-types-layout`
10. `port-emit`
11. `port-parser`
12. `port-macro`
13. `port-codegen` (may split into 2-3 steps)
14. `port-compile-main`
15. `cutover-remove-c`
16. `plsw-self-host-plan`: write the phase 5 plan as a new saga

## Open Questions

- Should the HLASM sources live in `hlasm/` in this repo (as proposed)
  or under `src/` once the C is removed?
- Is byte-identical `.s` output the right acceptance bar, or should
  semantically equivalent output (same program behavior) be allowed so
  the port can improve codegen along the way? This plan assumes
  byte-identical, so the port changes nothing.
- Should `components/linker` (Rust, host-side `link24`) be part of the
  native chain, or stay a host tool until phase 5?

## System services plan (storage, printing, buffer I/O)

Ported programs and plsw need the same handful of services. They are
provided as an hlasm macro library with **one interface and per-target
implementation members**. The target is chosen by which member the program
COPYs or INCLUDEs.

### Interface (macros)

| Macro | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GETMAIN reg,size` / `FREEMAIN reg,size` | storage from an arena (bump allocator with a free list) |
| `PUTC reg`, `PUTS label`, `PUTDEC reg`, `PUTHEX reg`, `PUTNL` | console output |
| `GETC reg`, `GETLINE buf,len` | console input |
| `WTO 'text'` | write a literal message (string emitted out of line with `\@`) |
| `DCB name,...` | control block for a named buffer ("file"): base, length, position, flags (laid out with M6 DSECT) |
| `OPEN dcb` / `CLOSE dcb` / `GET dcb,reg` / `PUT dcb,reg` / `READ dcb,buf,len` / `WRITE dcb,buf,len` | buffer I/O |
| `EXIT code` | terminate |

### Targets

- **`svc_bare.hlasm`** (bare metal, cor24-emu or the FPGA):
  - Console uses UART MMIO directly: data at 0xFF0100, status at 0xFF0101,
    polling the TX-busy bit.
  - GETMAIN draws on a static arena.
  - Input files are preloaded memory buffers (`--load-binary f@addr`, as
    hlasm's own sources are) or arrive over the UART framing protocol
    below.
  - `EXIT` spins (`bra` to self), which is the hardware halt idiom.
- **`svc_swtos.hlasm`** (sw-tos):
  - Calls go through the generated glue stubs only.
  - Console uses IPC to the TTY server (MSG_TTY_WRITE=1,
    MSG_TTY_READ_LINE=2, via SYS_SENDREC=5).
  - `EXIT` uses SYS_EXIT=2.
  - GETMAIN uses the sw-tos allocator.
  - Until sw-tos has a filesystem, a "file" is a named buffer. The DCB
    interface is unchanged when the filesystem module arrives.

Choosing the target by COPY needs nothing new from hlasm beyond the lifts
above (L8, L10, M1, M2). M3 lets one member hold both targets behind
`IFDEF`. Separate compilation through sw-tos's `link24` is a later option.
hlasm's output is plain `.s`, which link24 already consumes, so the services
could become a prebuilt module rather than COPYed source.

### UART framing protocol (batch I/O over one serial line)

To run in the emulator or on hardware, a compiler-like program (plsw,
hlasm itself later) needs several named inputs and one structured output
over a single UART. The protocol already used by
`sw-cor24-plsw/src/main.c` and `sw-tos/scripts/catalog-spawn-link.sh` is
adopted unchanged, so an HLASM-built plsw is a drop-in replacement.

Input (host to program):

```
c\n                                    mode line: c = compile, r = REPL (case-insensitive)
FILE:<name>\n<content>\x1E             zero or more named members (RS terminates each)
SOURCE:\n<content>\x04                 main source; \x04 (EOT) ends input, \x03 aborts
```

- Header lines (`FILE:...`, `SOURCE:`) are at most 80 characters.
- `\x04` or `\x03` inside a FILE member is an error.
- Legacy form: raw source followed by `\x04`, with no `SOURCE:` prefix.

Output (program to host):

```
<banner and prompt>
  registered: <name>                   one line per FILE member
--- generated assembly ---
<.s text>
--- end assembly ---
```

On failure the output is `ERROR: <message>` lines and
`--- compilation failed ---`. The host script greps for the error and end
markers and extracts the `.s` between the markers.

Library support:
- `UFRAME_READ` reads the mode line and the members into GETMAIN'd
  buffers and registers each FILE as a DCB, so `OPEN name` works on it.
- `UFRAME_BEGIN` / `UFRAME_END` / `UFRAME_FAIL` emit the markers.
- The same framing is the planned host interface for hlasm itself. It
  would replace the host-side `.bin`, config-block, and `--load-binary`
  path for users who only have a serial line (see L19).

Ordered so that the tiny-C ports (steps after these) have correct

input.description: Check agentrail insert usage

content.content:
Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

Usage: agentrail insert [OPTIONS] --after <AFTER> --slug <SLUG> --prompt <PROMPT>

Options:
      --after <AFTER>
          Position to insert after (0 prepends). The new step becomes N+1

      --slug <SLUG>
          Slug for the new step

      --prompt <PROMPT>
          Step prompt: text, file path, or "-" for stdin

      --role <ROLE>
          Step role (production, deterministic, validation, meta)
          
          [default: production]

      --task-type <TASK_TYPE>
          Task type for skill/trajectory lookup

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

input.content:
# Porting the tiny-C demos to hlasm

Status: plan (2026-11-07, saga `tinyc-macro-ports` step 9).

This plan covers porting the example programs in
`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos`, written in C and compiled by tc24r, to hlasm
source that uses a shared macro library. It is the porting method that
`sw-cor24-plsw/docs/migrate-from-c-to-hlasm.md` reuses for the PL/SW
compiler, so the calling convention, library layout and gap list here
are meant to carry over unchanged.

The user-facing write-up of the finished ports is
[c-demos-in-hlasm.md](c-demos-in-hlasm.md).

## What was surveyed

`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos` holds 69 C programs:

- `demo.c` and `demo2.c` through `demo64.c`;
- `hello.c`, `uart_tx.c`, `led.c` and `button.c`.

58 of them have tc24r output checked in as `.s`, and 64 have a
`run-demoN.sh` script. Almost every numbered demo is a self-test with the
same shape: `main` runs a set of checks, prints `DnOK` on the UART if they
all pass, and returns a known value, usually 42 (51-59 and 62-63 return
their own number). The run script checks that the CPU halted, that r0
holds that value, and that the UART log contains the marker.

Each demo was written to exercise one tc24r front-end feature, and that
shapes the port: many of them test C syntax that has no counterpart in
assembly (typedef, line continuation, tentative definitions). Those are
skipped; see [Demos to skip](#demos-to-skip).

## 1. Recurring idioms

Counts are from the 58 checked-in `.s` files.

### UART output

Every demo that prints defines its own `putc` and `puts`, or gets
`_putc_uart`/`puts` from `<stdio.h>`. `__putc_uart` is the most called
routine in the corpus (522 call sites):

```c
void putc(int c) { while (*(char *)0xFF0101 & 0x80) {} *(char *)0xFF0100 = c; }
void puts(char *s) { while (*s) { putc(*s); s = s + 1; } }
```

tc24r turns the 2-line `putc` into a 27-instruction routine, with a full
frame and a push/pop around each constant load. As a macro it is 5
instructions inline (see `PUTC` below).

### Decimal and hex printing

`printf` (`<stdio.h>`) is split by tc24r into `__tc24r_printf0..3`,
which call `_fmt_one`, which calls `_print_int`, `_print_hex` and
`_print_str`. 22 demos include `<stdio.h>`, but most use only `puts`;
demo39 and the Lisp demos use `%d`.

### LED and button

`LED_REG` 0xFF0000 is active-low: write 0 to turn LED D2 on. The button
is S2, bit 0 of the same address, which reads 0 while pressed. They are
used by `led.c`, `button.c`, demo2, demo8 and demo10.

### Function frame and calls (tc24r calling convention)

The hlasm library adopts this convention exactly, so HLASM routines and
tc24r routines can call each other. This is needed for the plsw hybrid
build.

```
caller:  push argN ... push arg1     (arguments right to left, one word each)
         la   r0,_fn
         jal  r1,(r0)
         add  sp,3*N                 (caller pops its arguments)
callee:  push fp / push r2 / push r1 / mov fp,sp     (prologue)
         sub  sp,LOCALS              (locals below fp, if any)
         arg1 at 9(fp), arg2 at 12(fp), ...; locals at -3(fp), -6(fp), ...
         result in r0
         mov sp,fp / pop r1 / pop r2 / pop fp / jmp (r1)  (epilogue)
```

- r0 and r1 are scratch. r2 is preserved by the prologue and epilogue,
  so a callee may use it freely.
- Labels are the C name with a leading `_`. `_start` calls `_main` and
  then spins on `_halt: bra _halt`.
- Frames are adjusted with `add sp,±n` up to 127 and `sub sp,n` beyond
  that: demo50's 256-byte local buffer uses `sub sp,259`.
  `lw`/`sw` offsets are 8-bit, so locals beyond -128(fp) need an address
  computed with `mov`/`add`. That was tc24r's BUG-013.

### Compare and branch

tc24r compares with `ceq`, `cls` and `clu`, branches with `brt`/`brf`, and
materialises every comparison result as 0/1 before testing it. Those are
the hlasm structured conditions `cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt` and `cc_lu`.
C also uses `<=`, `>` and `>=`, signed and unsigned (demo46 is all of
them). hlasm has no direct form for these yet; see gap T1.

### Loops

C `while`, `do`/`while` and `for` are all `DO ... DOEXIT ... ENDDO`.
`continue` is `ITERATE` and `break` is `DOEXIT` with no operands.
`for (i = a; i < b; i++)` has an initialiser before `DO` and an increment
before `ENDDO`. `continue` in a `for` loop must still run the increment,
so the increment goes at the top of the next pass or `ITERATE` targets a
label before it. demo13 shows both cases.

### Self-test checks

Nearly every demo is a list of `if (x != expected) { ok = 0; }` lines, or
calls to a `check(cond, id)` helper (demo46). This is the most repeated
source pattern in the corpus, and a `CHECK` macro makes each line one
statement (see the API below).

### Multiply, divide, modulo

COR24 has `mul` but no divide. tc24r emits `__tc24r_div` and
`__tc24r_mod` routines (25 and 36 call sites; demo4, demo13 and the
`%`-heavy demos). The library provides them as routines, with `DIV`/`MOD`
macros that call them.

### Arrays and pointers

- Element addressing is `base + i*3` for `int` and `base + i` for `char`,
  computed with `shl`/`add` or `mul`.
- Pointer subtraction divides by 3 (demo7).
- Global arrays are `.word`/`.byte` lists or `.space`.
- Multi-dimensional arrays are row-major (demo34).

### Structs and unions

Member access is `base + offset`. Offsets come from the declaration
order: one word per `int` and pointer, one byte per `char`, and arrays
of members are counted in full (demo35). Union members all have offset
0. In hlasm the offsets are `EQU` symbols computed with expressions,
until M6 DSECT/FIELD exists.

### Strings and data

- String literals become `_Sn: .byte ...,0` in `.data`.
- Globals with initialisers become `.word`/`.byte` lists (demo58).
- Adjacent literals are joined (demo63).
- hlasm already turns `.ascii "text\n"` into a `.byte` list with escapes
  resolved, and a macro body can switch to `.data` and back to `.text`.
  That is enough for out-of-line string literals; both were verified
  during this survey.

### Heap

`<stdlib.h>` `malloc` is a bump allocator over a static arena, and `free`
does nothing. demo40, demo43, demo44 and demo45 use it. This maps onto
`GETMAIN`/`FREEMAIN` in the services interface.

### Function pointers

These are `la r0,_fn` stored in a word and called as `jal r1,(r0)`
(demo51-54). They need no macro beyond `CALL` accepting a register or
memory operand as the target.

### Interrupts

demo9 installs an interrupt handler: `la r0,_isr` / `mov iv,r0`, enable
at 0xFF0010, and the handler returns with `jmp (ir)`. hlasm passes these
lines through unchanged, so no macro is needed.

## 2. Macro library API and layout

### COPY member layout

The library lives under `lib/`. A program pulls members in with `COPY`
through its `.sourceset`, and `demos/tinyc/lib.sourceset` lists them
once for all ports:

| Member | Contents | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/cor24.hlasm` | `EQU`s for the board: `UART_DATA`, `UART_STATUS`, `UART_TXBUSY`, `LED_REG`, `INT_ENABLE`, `LED_ON`, `LED_OFF` | symbols only |
| `lib/frame.hlasm` | `PROLOG`, `RET`, `RETURN`, `CALL`, `ARG`, `LOCAL`, `START` | macros only |
| `lib/svc_bare.hlasm` | services interface, bare-metal target: `PUTC`, `PUTS`, `PUTDEC`, `PUTHEX`, `PUTNL`, `WTO`, `GETC`, `GETLINE`, `GETMAIN`, `FREEMAIN`, `EXIT` | macros |
| `lib/svc_bare_rt.hlasm` | the routines those macros call: `_svc_puts`, `_svc_putdec`, `_svc_puthex`, `_svc_getc`, `_svc_getline`, `_svc_getmain` and the arena | code |
| `lib/board.hlasm` | `LEDON`, `LEDOFF`, `BUTTON reg` | macros |
| `lib/rt.hlasm` | runtime routines: `_div`, `_mod`, `_strlen`, `_strcmp`, `_strcpy`, `_memcpy`, `_memset`, `_atoi`, plus `DIV`/`MOD` macros | code and macros |
| `lib/data.hlasm` | `STR label,"text"` (a NUL-terminated string in `.data`), `WORDS label,v1,...`, `BYTES label,v1,...`, `SPACE label,n` | macros |
| `lib/check.hlasm` | `CHECKINIT`, `CHECK cond,a,b`, `CHECKEND 'marker',rc`: the self-test pattern | macros |

Rules:

- **Macros-only members** (`cor24`, `frame`, `svc_bare`, `board`, `data`,
  `check`) can be COPYed at the top of any program, because they emit no
  code until they are called.
- **Code members** (`svc_bare_rt`, `rt`) are COPYed at the end, after the
  program's own routines. Each routine sits inside `IFDEF NEED_<name>`.
  The macros that call a routine `SET NEED_<name>,1`, so only routines
  that were used are emitted. tc24r does the same job with a dead-code
  pass, which demo64 checks. Conditional assembly does it here, which is
  one of the macro features the showcase demonstrates.
- **Each member has an include guard** (`IFNDEF LIB_<member>` /
  `SET LIB_<member>,1`), so a member listed twice is harmless.
- **Library labels** are `_svc_*`, `_rt_*` or the C library name (`_strlen`)
  where a tc24r program would call it. Macro-local labels use `\@`.
- **Choosing the target.** The services interface is the one in
  [limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md#system-services-plan-storage-printing-buffer-io).
  A later `lib/svc_swtos.hlasm` provides the same macros over sw-tos IPC.
  A program chooses its target by which member it COPYs; nothing else
  changes.

### Macro reference (proposed)

Register effects follow the calling convention: macros may clobber r0
and r1 and preserve r2 unless stated.

| Macro | Expands to | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PROLOG [locals]` | `push fp`/`push r2`/`push r1`/`mov fp,sp`; then `add sp,-n` (n ≤ 127) or `sub sp,n` | locals in bytes, default 0 |
| `RET` | `mov sp,fp`/`pop r1`/`pop r2`/`pop fp`/`jmp (r1)` | result already in r0 |
| `RETURN value` | load value into r0, then `RET` | |
| `ARG reg,n` | `lw reg,9+3*(n-1)(fp)` | nth argument (1-based) |
| `LOCAL name,bytes` | `name EQU -offset` from a running `SET` counter; `PROLOG` uses the total | named locals as fp offsets |
| `CALL fn[,a1,...,a8]` | push the arguments right to left (a constant or label with `la r0,`, a register with `push`), `la r0,fn`/`jal r1,(r0)`, then `add sp,3*N` | result in r0 |
| `START [main]` | `_start: la r0,_main`/`jal r1,(r0)`, an optional r0 report, `_halt: bra _halt` | program entry |
| `PUTC [reg]` | wait for TX not busy, `sb reg,0(UART)` (inline, 5 instructions plus `push`/`pop r2`) | default r0 |
| `PUTS label\|reg` | `CALL _svc_puts,arg` | NUL-terminated string |
| `PUTDEC reg`, `PUTHEX reg` | `CALL _svc_putdec`/`_svc_puthex` | signed decimal; 6 hex digits |
| `PUTNL` | `PUTC` of 10 | |
| `WTO "text"` | the string out of line in `.data` (`S\@`), then `PUTS S\@` | escapes resolved by hlasm |
| `GETC reg` | `CALL _svc_getc` | -1 at EOF (0x04) |
| `GETLINE buf,len` | `CALL _svc_getline` | length in r0 |
| `GETMAIN reg,size` / `FREEMAIN reg,size` | bump allocation from the arena / no-op (as tc24r's `free`) | |
| `EXIT [code]` | load code into r0, `bra _halt` | |
| `LEDON` / `LEDOFF` / `BUTTON reg` | `sb` 0/1 to `LED_REG`; `lb reg`, mask bit 0 | |
| `DIV a,b` / `MOD a,b` | `CALL _div,a,b` / `CALL _mod,a,b` | signed, truncating like C |
| `STR label,"text"` | `.data`/`label: .ascii "text"`/`.byte 0`/`.text` | |
| `CHECKINIT` / `CHECK cond,a,b` / `CHECKEND 'DnOK',rc` | clear an ok flag when `cond a,b` is false; at the end print the marker and return rc if all checks passed, else return 0 | the demo self-test |

**Result checking.** The tc24r run scripts check r0 through
`cor24-emu --dump`, but the hlasm e2e harness checks UART output only.
`START` therefore prints `r0=<n>` after `_main` returns when `SET
SHOWRC,1` is in effect, and every port turns it on. A port's expected
output is the C demo's marker followed by `r0=42` (or the demo's own
value), which checks the same two things the tc24r run script does.

## 3. Which demos to port

The order runs from simple to complex. Each group is one saga step, and
every port gets an `hlasm_e2e_tinyc_<demo>` reg-rs test.

### Group A: I/O (step `port-io-demos`)

| Demo | Shows | Library |
|---|---|---|
| `uart_tx` | raw UART writes | `PUTC` |
| `hello` | string iteration | `PUTS`, `STR`, `START` |
| `led` | LED on | `LEDON` |
| `button` | read S2 and show it on the LED | `BUTTON`, `LEDON`/`LEDOFF`, run with `--switch on` |
| `demo2` | char, pointers, MMIO, prints `OK` | `cor24` `EQU`s, `CHECK` |
| `demo3` | hex literals, pointer walk over a string | `STR`, `PUTS` |
| `demo8` | `#define` constants | `EQU` |
| `demo10` | `#include` and a system header | `COPY` of a demo-local member |
| `demo64` | no-std: copy "hello" to memory and halt | no services at all; shows that unused library routines are not emitted |
| `demo9` | UART RX interrupt | raw `iv`/`ir` lines, run with `-u A` |

### Group B: control flow (step `port-control-flow-demos`)

| Demo | Shows | hlasm construct |
|---|---|---|
| `demo` | functions, recursion (fib), while and for loops, bit operations | `PROLOG`/`CALL`/`RET`, `DO` |
| `demo4` | software divide and modulo | `DIV`/`MOD`, `lib/rt` |
| `demo11` | `&&` and `\|\|` with short-circuit | nested `IF` (until M5) |
| `demo12` | do...while | `DO` with `DOEXIT` at the end |
| `demo13` | break and continue | `DOEXIT`, `ITERATE` |
| `demo14` | `++` and `--` | `add reg,±1`, with no macro needed |
| `demo15` | ternary `?:` | `IF`/`ELSE` |
| `demo21` | compound assignment | plain instructions |
| `demo26` | switch/case | `SELECT`/`WHEN`/`OTHERWISE` |
| `demo46` | signed and unsigned comparisons and shifts | `cc_lt`/`cc_lu`, plus the T1 forms |

### Group C: functions, arrays, pointers, strings (step `port-function-and-data-demos`)

| Demo | Shows |
|---|---|
| `demo5` | arrays: declaration, indexing, decay to pointer |
| `demo6` | global char, pointer and array patterns |
| `demo7` | pointer subtraction |
| `demo16` | character literals (`'a'`, `'\n'`) |
| `demo39` | printf `%d` |
| `demo41` | getc (`-u` input), atoi, strlen/strcmp/strcpy |
| `demo50` | a 256-byte local array with nested calls (frames beyond 127 bytes) |
| `demo51`-`demo53` | function pointers: a variable, a dispatch table, a parameter |
| `demo58` | global data initialisation |
| `demo63` | adjacent string literals |

### Group D: structs, unions and the heap (step `port-struct-and-heap-demos`, inserted)

Group C plus this group came to 22 demos, too many for one step, so the
function/data step was split.

| Demo | Shows |
|---|---|
| `demo23` | enum, as `EQU` |
| `demo25` | struct members, `sizeof` |
| `demo28` | union |
| `demo34` | 2-D arrays |
| `demo35` | arrays inside structs |
| `demo38` | struct initialiser as data |
| `demo40` | malloc/free |
| `demo42` | linked list, chained `->` |
| `demo43` | cons cells: malloc'd structs returned by pointer |

The showcase step may add demo44 (the Lisp printer, 155 lines) as a
larger example if time allows. demo45 (the Lisp evaluator, 300 lines) is
the stretch goal.

### Demos to skip

The skipped demos test C syntax that a programmer writing assembly never
meets, or they repeat a group above:

| Demo | Why skipped |
|---|---|
| demo17 multi-declaration, demo24 typedef, demo30 line continuation, demo31 tentative definitions, demo32 multi-declarator typedef, demo33 comma-separated members, demo36 forward struct tags, demo37 anonymous members, demo22 braceless bodies | C syntax only: they compile to the same code as other demos |
| demo18 and demo29 sizeof, demo55 and demo62 constant expressions in array sizes | covered by `EQU` expressions inside the Group C/D ports |
| demo19 static/extern, demo27 prototypes | no assembly meaning: there is one label namespace, and forward references are free |
| demo20 statement expressions, demo60 compound literals | C extensions with no assembly counterpart |
| demo47, demo48, demo49, demo56, demo57, demo59 | tc24r parser regression tests (BUG-003, -010 to -013) that repeat the struct and array accesses already in Group D |
| demo61 inline asm | the whole program is already assembly |
| demo44, demo45 | large; showcase candidates (see above), not part of the port steps |

That is 39 demos ported and 30 skipped.

## 4. Feature gaps

Cross-checked against
[limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md) (L, D and M
items) and the plsw migration plan (B and G items). Each gap was checked
by running a small program through `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh`.

### Resolved before this plan

These are already done in hlasm, so the library can rely on them:

- **B5/M3: directives inside macro bodies.** Verified: a `CALL` macro
  that pushes 0-3 arguments using `IFEQ &SYSNARG,n`, and pops them with
  `add sp,(&SYSNARG-1)*3`, ran correctly.
- **B6/M2: default parameters.** `PUTC &R=r0` works.
- **Out-of-line data from a macro.** A `WTO` body that switches to `.data`,
  emits `S\@: .ascii "..."`, switches back and calls `_puts` ran correctly,
  with `\n` and `\t` resolved.
- **Large frames.** `sub sp,n` takes a 24-bit immediate, so `PROLOG`
  needs no conditional for frames beyond 127 bytes.

### New gaps that block the library (inserted as step `condition-forms-and-arg-tests`)

| # | Gap | Found | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Structured conditions have no `<=`, `>`, `>=` forms (`cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge`, and unsigned `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`) | most Group B demos; demo46 uses all of them | Without them every C relational operator becomes swapped operands plus an extra register load, or an inverted `IF ... ELSE`. That is exactly the noise the showcase argues macros remove |
| T2 | Conditional assembly cannot classify a macro argument. There is no text comparison (HLASM `AIF ('&A' EQ 'r2')`), and an undefined name in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` silently evaluates to 0, so `IFEQ &A,r2` is true for any argument that is not a symbol | testing `CALL` | `CALL fn,r2,5,_buf` must `push r2` for a register but `la r0,5`/`push r0` for a constant or label. Without a test it needs separate macros per argument kind, which defeats the point of a single `CALL` |

The inserted step adds the six condition forms to IF/ELSEIF/DOEXIT/WHEN,
plus a text test for conditional assembly (for example `IFSAME a,b` /
`IFDIFF a,b`, or quoted-string comparison in `IFEQ`/`IFNE`). It also
decides whether an undefined symbol in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` becomes an ERROR,
checking the existing demos first.

### Known gaps that do not block the ports

| # | Gap | Workaround in the ports | Planned |
|---|---|---|---|

# Porting the tiny-C demos to hlasm

Status: plan (2026-11-07, saga `tinyc-macro-ports` step 9).

This plan covers porting the example programs in
`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos`, written in C and compiled by tc24r, to hlasm
source that uses a shared macro library. It is the porting method that
`sw-cor24-plsw/docs/migrate-from-c-to-hlasm.md` reuses for the PL/SW
compiler, so the calling convention, library layout and gap list here
are meant to carry over unchanged.

The user-facing write-up of the finished ports is
[c-demos-in-hlasm.md](c-demos-in-hlasm.md).

## What was surveyed

`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos` holds 69 C programs:

- `demo.c` and `demo2.c` through `demo64.c`;
- `hello.c`, `uart_tx.c`, `led.c` and `button.c`.

58 of them have tc24r output checked in as `.s`, and 64 have a
`run-demoN.sh` script. Almost every numbered demo is a self-test with the
same shape: `main` runs a set of checks, prints `DnOK` on the UART if they
all pass, and returns a known value, usually 42 (51-59 and 62-63 return
their own number). The run script checks that the CPU halted, that r0
holds that value, and that the UART log contains the marker.

Each demo was written to exercise one tc24r front-end feature, and that
shapes the port: many of them test C syntax that has no counterpart in
assembly (typedef, line continuation, tentative definitions). Those are
skipped; see [Demos to skip](#demos-to-skip).

## 1. Recurring idioms

Counts are from the 58 checked-in `.s` files.

### UART output

Every demo that prints defines its own `putc` and `puts`, or gets
`_putc_uart`/`puts` from `<stdio.h>`. `__putc_uart` is the most called
routine in the corpus (522 call sites):

```c
void putc(int c) { while (*(char *)0xFF0101 & 0x80) {} *(char *)0xFF0100 = c; }
void puts(char *s) { while (*s) { putc(*s); s = s + 1; } }
```

tc24r turns the 2-line `putc` into a 27-instruction routine, with a full
frame and a push/pop around each constant load. As a macro it is 5
instructions inline (see `PUTC` below).

### Decimal and hex printing

`printf` (`<stdio.h>`) is split by tc24r into `__tc24r_printf0..3`,
which call `_fmt_one`, which calls `_print_int`, `_print_hex` and
`_print_str`. 22 demos include `<stdio.h>`, but most use only `puts`;
demo39 and the Lisp demos use `%d`.

### LED and button

`LED_REG` 0xFF0000 is active-low: write 0 to turn LED D2 on. The button
is S2, bit 0 of the same address, which reads 0 while pressed. They are
used by `led.c`, `button.c`, demo2, demo8 and demo10.

### Function frame and calls (tc24r calling convention)

The hlasm library adopts this convention exactly, so HLASM routines and
tc24r routines can call each other. This is needed for the plsw hybrid
build.

```
caller:  push argN ... push arg1     (arguments right to left, one word each)
         la   r0,_fn
         jal  r1,(r0)
         add  sp,3*N                 (caller pops its arguments)
callee:  push fp / push r2 / push r1 / mov fp,sp     (prologue)
         sub  sp,LOCALS              (locals below fp, if any)
         arg1 at 9(fp), arg2 at 12(fp), ...; locals at -3(fp), -6(fp), ...
         result in r0
         mov sp,fp / pop r1 / pop r2 / pop fp / jmp (r1)  (epilogue)
```

- r0 and r1 are scratch. r2 is preserved by the prologue and epilogue,
  so a callee may use it freely.
- Labels are the C name with a leading `_`. `_start` calls `_main` and
  then spins on `_halt: bra _halt`.
- Frames are adjusted with `add sp,±n` up to 127 and `sub sp,n` beyond
  that: demo50's 256-byte local buffer uses `sub sp,259`.
  `lw`/`sw` offsets are 8-bit, so locals beyond -128(fp) need an address
  computed with `mov`/`add`. That was tc24r's BUG-013.

### Compare and branch

tc24r compares with `ceq`, `cls` and `clu`, branches with `brt`/`brf`, and
materialises every comparison result as 0/1 before testing it. Those are
the hlasm structured conditions `cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt` and `cc_lu`.
C also uses `<=`, `>` and `>=`, signed and unsigned (demo46 is all of
them). hlasm has no direct form for these yet; see gap T1.

### Loops

C `while`, `do`/`while` and `for` are all `DO ... DOEXIT ... ENDDO`.
`continue` is `ITERATE` and `break` is `DOEXIT` with no operands.
`for (i = a; i < b; i++)` has an initialiser before `DO` and an increment
before `ENDDO`. `continue` in a `for` loop must still run the increment,
so the increment goes at the top of the next pass or `ITERATE` targets a
label before it. demo13 shows both cases.

### Self-test checks

Nearly every demo is a list of `if (x != expected) { ok = 0; }` lines, or
calls to a `check(cond, id)` helper (demo46). This is the most repeated
source pattern in the corpus, and a `CHECK` macro makes each line one
statement (see the API below).

### Multiply, divide, modulo

COR24 has `mul` but no divide. tc24r emits `__tc24r_div` and
`__tc24r_mod` routines (25 and 36 call sites; demo4, demo13 and the
`%`-heavy demos). The library provides them as routines, with `DIV`/`MOD`
macros that call them.

### Arrays and pointers

- Element addressing is `base + i*3` for `int` and `base + i` for `char`,
  computed with `shl`/`add` or `mul`.
- Pointer subtraction divides by 3 (demo7).
- Global arrays are `.word`/`.byte` lists or `.space`.
- Multi-dimensional arrays are row-major (demo34).

### Structs and unions

Member access is `base + offset`. Offsets come from the declaration
order: one word per `int` and pointer, one byte per `char`, and arrays
of members are counted in full (demo35). Union members all have offset
0. In hlasm the offsets are `EQU` symbols computed with expressions,
until M6 DSECT/FIELD exists.

### Strings and data

- String literals become `_Sn: .byte ...,0` in `.data`.
- Globals with initialisers become `.word`/`.byte` lists (demo58).
- Adjacent literals are joined (demo63).
- hlasm already turns `.ascii "text\n"` into a `.byte` list with escapes
  resolved, and a macro body can switch to `.data` and back to `.text`.
  That is enough for out-of-line string literals; both were verified
  during this survey.

### Heap

`<stdlib.h>` `malloc` is a bump allocator over a static arena, and `free`
does nothing. demo40, demo43, demo44 and demo45 use it. This maps onto
`GETMAIN`/`FREEMAIN` in the services interface.

### Function pointers

These are `la r0,_fn` stored in a word and called as `jal r1,(r0)`
(demo51-54). They need no macro beyond `CALL` accepting a register or
memory operand as the target.

### Interrupts

demo9 installs an interrupt handler: `la r0,_isr` / `mov iv,r0`, enable
at 0xFF0010, and the handler returns with `jmp (ir)`. hlasm passes these
lines through unchanged, so no macro is needed.

## 2. Macro library API and layout

### COPY member layout

The library lives under `lib/`. A program pulls members in with `COPY`
through its `.sourceset`, and `demos/tinyc/lib.sourceset` lists them
once for all ports:

| Member | Contents | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/cor24.hlasm` | `EQU`s for the board: `UART_DATA`, `UART_STATUS`, `UART_TXBUSY`, `LED_REG`, `INT_ENABLE`, `LED_ON`, `LED_OFF` | symbols only |
| `lib/frame.hlasm` | `PROLOG`, `RET`, `RETURN`, `CALL`, `ARG`, `LOCAL`, `START` | macros only |
| `lib/svc_bare.hlasm` | services interface, bare-metal target: `PUTC`, `PUTS`, `PUTDEC`, `PUTHEX`, `PUTNL`, `WTO`, `GETC`, `GETLINE`, `GETMAIN`, `FREEMAIN`, `EXIT` | macros |
| `lib/svc_bare_rt.hlasm` | the routines those macros call: `_svc_puts`, `_svc_putdec`, `_svc_puthex`, `_svc_getc`, `_svc_getline`, `_svc_getmain` and the arena | code |
| `lib/board.hlasm` | `LEDON`, `LEDOFF`, `BUTTON reg` | macros |
| `lib/rt.hlasm` | runtime routines: `_div`, `_mod`, `_strlen`, `_strcmp`, `_strcpy`, `_memcpy`, `_memset`, `_atoi`, plus `DIV`/`MOD` macros | code and macros |
| `lib/data.hlasm` | `STR label,"text"` (a NUL-terminated string in `.data`), `WORDS label,v1,...`, `BYTES label,v1,...`, `SPACE label,n` | macros |
| `lib/check.hlasm` | `CHECKINIT`, `CHECK cond,a,b`, `CHECKEND 'marker',rc`: the self-test pattern | macros |

Rules:

- **Macros-only members** (`cor24`, `frame`, `svc_bare`, `board`, `data`,
  `check`) can be COPYed at the top of any program, because they emit no
  code until they are called.
- **Code members** (`svc_bare_rt`, `rt`) are COPYed at the end, after the
  program's own routines. Each routine sits inside `IFDEF NEED_<name>`.
  The macros that call a routine `SET NEED_<name>,1`, so only routines
  that were used are emitted. tc24r does the same job with a dead-code
  pass, which demo64 checks. Conditional assembly does it here, which is
  one of the macro features the showcase demonstrates.
- **Each member has an include guard** (`IFNDEF LIB_<member>` /
  `SET LIB_<member>,1`), so a member listed twice is harmless.
- **Library labels** are `_svc_*`, `_rt_*` or the C library name (`_strlen`)
  where a tc24r program would call it. Macro-local labels use `\@`.
- **Choosing the target.** The services interface is the one in
  [limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md#system-services-plan-storage-printing-buffer-io).
  A later `lib/svc_swtos.hlasm` provides the same macros over sw-tos IPC.
  A program chooses its target by which member it COPYs; nothing else
  changes.

### Macro reference (proposed)

Register effects follow the calling convention: macros may clobber r0
and r1 and preserve r2 unless stated.

| Macro | Expands to | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PROLOG [locals]` | `push fp`/`push r2`/`push r1`/`mov fp,sp`; then `add sp,-n` (n ≤ 127) or `sub sp,n` | locals in bytes, default 0 |
| `RET` | `mov sp,fp`/`pop r1`/`pop r2`/`pop fp`/`jmp (r1)` | result already in r0 |
| `RETURN value` | load value into r0, then `RET` | |
| `ARG reg,n` | `lw reg,9+3*(n-1)(fp)` | nth argument (1-based) |
| `LOCAL name,bytes` | `name EQU -offset` from a running `SET` counter; `PROLOG` uses the total | named locals as fp offsets |
| `CALL fn[,a1,...,a8]` | push the arguments right to left (a constant or label with `la r0,`, a register with `push`), `la r0,fn`/`jal r1,(r0)`, then `add sp,3*N` | result in r0 |
| `START [main]` | `_start: la r0,_main`/`jal r1,(r0)`, an optional r0 report, `_halt: bra _halt` | program entry |
| `PUTC [reg]` | wait for TX not busy, `sb reg,0(UART)` (inline, 5 instructions plus `push`/`pop r2`) | default r0 |
| `PUTS label\|reg` | `CALL _svc_puts,arg` | NUL-terminated string |
| `PUTDEC reg`, `PUTHEX reg` | `CALL _svc_putdec`/`_svc_puthex` | signed decimal; 6 hex digits |
| `PUTNL` | `PUTC` of 10 | |
| `WTO "text"` | the string out of line in `.data` (`S\@`), then `PUTS S\@` | escapes resolved by hlasm |
| `GETC reg` | `CALL _svc_getc` | -1 at EOF (0x04) |
| `GETLINE buf,len` | `CALL _svc_getline` | length in r0 |
| `GETMAIN reg,size` / `FREEMAIN reg,size` | bump allocation from the arena / no-op (as tc24r's `free`) | |
| `EXIT [code]` | load code into r0, `bra _halt` | |
| `LEDON` / `LEDOFF` / `BUTTON reg` | `sb` 0/1 to `LED_REG`; `lb reg`, mask bit 0 | |
| `DIV a,b` / `MOD a,b` | `CALL _div,a,b` / `CALL _mod,a,b` | signed, truncating like C |
| `STR label,"text"` | `.data`/`label: .ascii "text"`/`.byte 0`/`.text` | |
| `CHECKINIT` / `CHECK cond,a,b` / `CHECKEND 'DnOK',rc` | clear an ok flag when `cond a,b` is false; at the end print the marker and return rc if all checks passed, else return 0 | the demo self-test |

**Result checking.** The tc24r run scripts check r0 through
`cor24-emu --dump`, but the hlasm e2e harness checks UART output only.
`START` therefore prints `r0=<n>` after `_main` returns when `SET
SHOWRC,1` is in effect, and every port turns it on. A port's expected
output is the C demo's marker followed by `r0=42` (or the demo's own
value), which checks the same two things the tc24r run script does.

## 3. Which demos to port

The order runs from simple to complex. Each group is one saga step, and
every port gets an `hlasm_e2e_tinyc_<demo>` reg-rs test.

### Group A: I/O (step `port-io-demos`)

| Demo | Shows | Library |
|---|---|---|
| `uart_tx` | raw UART writes | `PUTC` |
| `hello` | string iteration | `PUTS`, `STR`, `START` |
| `led` | LED on | `LEDON` |
| `button` | read S2 and show it on the LED | `BUTTON`, `LEDON`/`LEDOFF`, run with `--switch on` |
| `demo2` | char, pointers, MMIO, prints `OK` | `cor24` `EQU`s, `CHECK` |
| `demo3` | hex literals, pointer walk over a string | `STR`, `PUTS` |
| `demo8` | `#define` constants | `EQU` |
| `demo10` | `#include` and a system header | `COPY` of a demo-local member |
| `demo64` | no-std: copy "hello" to memory and halt | no services at all; shows that unused library routines are not emitted |
| `demo9` | UART RX interrupt | raw `iv`/`ir` lines, run with `-u A` |

### Group B: control flow (step `port-control-flow-demos`)

| Demo | Shows | hlasm construct |
|---|---|---|
| `demo` | functions, recursion (fib), while and for loops, bit operations | `PROLOG`/`CALL`/`RET`, `DO` |
| `demo4` | software divide and modulo | `DIV`/`MOD`, `lib/rt` |
| `demo11` | `&&` and `\|\|` with short-circuit | nested `IF` (until M5) |
| `demo12` | do...while | `DO` with `DOEXIT` at the end |
| `demo13` | break and continue | `DOEXIT`, `ITERATE` |
| `demo14` | `++` and `--` | `add reg,±1`, with no macro needed |
| `demo15` | ternary `?:` | `IF`/`ELSE` |
| `demo21` | compound assignment | plain instructions |
| `demo26` | switch/case | `SELECT`/`WHEN`/`OTHERWISE` |
| `demo46` | signed and unsigned comparisons and shifts | `cc_lt`/`cc_lu`, plus the T1 forms |

### Group C: functions, arrays, pointers, strings (step `port-function-and-data-demos`)

| Demo | Shows |
|---|---|
| `demo5` | arrays: declaration, indexing, decay to pointer |
| `demo6` | global char, pointer and array patterns |
| `demo7` | pointer subtraction |
| `demo16` | character literals (`'a'`, `'\n'`) |
| `demo39` | printf `%d` |
| `demo41` | getc (`-u` input), atoi, strlen/strcmp/strcpy |
| `demo50` | a 256-byte local array with nested calls (frames beyond 127 bytes) |
| `demo51`-`demo53` | function pointers: a variable, a dispatch table, a parameter |
| `demo58` | global data initialisation |
| `demo63` | adjacent string literals |

### Group D: structs, unions and the heap (step `port-struct-and-heap-demos`, inserted)

Group C plus this group came to 22 demos, too many for one step, so the
function/data step was split.

| Demo | Shows |
|---|---|
| `demo23` | enum, as `EQU` |
| `demo25` | struct members, `sizeof` |
| `demo28` | union |
| `demo34` | 2-D arrays |
| `demo35` | arrays inside structs |
| `demo38` | struct initialiser as data |
| `demo40` | malloc/free |
| `demo42` | linked list, chained `->` |
| `demo43` | cons cells: malloc'd structs returned by pointer |

The showcase step may add demo44 (the Lisp printer, 155 lines) as a
larger example if time allows. demo45 (the Lisp evaluator, 300 lines) is
the stretch goal.

### Demos to skip

The skipped demos test C syntax that a programmer writing assembly never
meets, or they repeat a group above:

| Demo | Why skipped |
|---|---|
| demo17 multi-declaration, demo24 typedef, demo30 line continuation, demo31 tentative definitions, demo32 multi-declarator typedef, demo33 comma-separated members, demo36 forward struct tags, demo37 anonymous members, demo22 braceless bodies | C syntax only: they compile to the same code as other demos |
| demo18 and demo29 sizeof, demo55 and demo62 constant expressions in array sizes | covered by `EQU` expressions inside the Group C/D ports |
| demo19 static/extern, demo27 prototypes | no assembly meaning: there is one label namespace, and forward references are free |
| demo20 statement expressions, demo60 compound literals | C extensions with no assembly counterpart |
| demo47, demo48, demo49, demo56, demo57, demo59 | tc24r parser regression tests (BUG-003, -010 to -013) that repeat the struct and array accesses already in Group D |
| demo61 inline asm | the whole program is already assembly |
| demo44, demo45 | large; showcase candidates (see above), not part of the port steps |

That is 39 demos ported and 30 skipped.

## 4. Feature gaps

Cross-checked against
[limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md) (L, D and M
items) and the plsw migration plan (B and G items). Each gap was checked
by running a small program through `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh`.

### Resolved before this plan

These are already done in hlasm, so the library can rely on them:

- **B5/M3: directives inside macro bodies.** Verified: a `CALL` macro
  that pushes 0-3 arguments using `IFEQ &SYSNARG,n`, and pops them with
  `add sp,(&SYSNARG-1)*3`, ran correctly.
- **B6/M2: default parameters.** `PUTC &R=r0` works.
- **Out-of-line data from a macro.** A `WTO` body that switches to `.data`,
  emits `S\@: .ascii "..."`, switches back and calls `_puts` ran correctly,
  with `\n` and `\t` resolved.
- **Large frames.** `sub sp,n` takes a 24-bit immediate, so `PROLOG`
  needs no conditional for frames beyond 127 bytes.

### New gaps that block the library (inserted as step `condition-forms-and-arg-tests`)

| # | Gap | Found | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Structured conditions have no `<=`, `>`, `>=` forms (`cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge`, and unsigned `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`) | most Group B demos; demo46 uses all of them | Without them every C relational operator becomes swapped operands plus an extra register load, or an inverted `IF ... ELSE`. That is exactly the noise the showcase argues macros remove |
| T2 | Conditional assembly cannot classify a macro argument. There is no text comparison (HLASM `AIF ('&A' EQ 'r2')`), and an undefined name in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` silently evaluates to 0, so `IFEQ &A,r2` is true for any argument that is not a symbol | testing `CALL` | `CALL fn,r2,5,_buf` must `push r2` for a register but `la r0,5`/`push r0` for a constant or label. Without a test it needs separate macros per argument kind, which defeats the point of a single `CALL` |

The inserted step adds the six condition forms to IF/ELSEIF/DOEXIT/WHEN,
plus a text test for conditional assembly (for example `IFSAME a,b` /
`IFDIFF a,b`, or quoted-string comparison in `IFEQ`/`IFNE`). It also
decides whether an undefined symbol in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` becomes an ERROR,
checking the existing demos first.

### Known gaps that do not block the ports

| # | Gap | Workaround in the ports | Planned |
|---|---|---|---|
| M5 / G1 | compound conditions (`AND`/`OR`) | nested `IF` (demo11) | plsw-readiness saga |
| M6 / G3 | DSECT/FIELD struct layout | `EQU` offsets with expressions (Group D) | plsw-readiness saga |
| D11 | cor24-asm rejects label arithmetic in `.word` | compute such addresses at run time | assembler issue |
| G7 | assembly time (two passes on the emulator) | none needed at demo size | later cost work |
| — | no `MACRO` definition or `INCLUDE`/`COPY` inside a macro body | not needed by the library | not planned |

Any new gap found during the port steps goes into this table and into
`limits-and-lifting-plan.md`. If it blocks a port, it gets its own saga
step (`agentrail insert`) rather than a workaround.
