  that: demo50's 256-byte local buffer uses `sub sp,259`.
  `lw`/`sw` offsets are 8-bit, so locals beyond -128(fp) need an address
  computed with `mov`/`add`. That was tc24r's BUG-013.

### Compare and branch

tc24r compares with `ceq`, `cls` and `clu`, branches with `brt`/`brf`, and
materialises every comparison result as 0/1 before testing it. Those are
the hlasm structured conditions `cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt` and `cc_lu`.
C also uses `<=`, `>` and `>=`, signed and unsigned (demo46 is all of
them). hlasm has no direct form for these yet; see gap T1.

### Loops

C `while`, `do`/`while` and `for` are all `DO ... DOEXIT ... ENDDO`.
`continue` is `ITERATE` and `break` is `DOEXIT` with no operands.
`for (i = a; i < b; i++)` has an initialiser before `DO` and an increment
before `ENDDO`. `continue` in a `for` loop must still run the increment,
so the increment goes at the top of the next pass or `ITERATE` targets a
label before it. demo13 shows both cases.

### Self-test checks

Nearly every demo is a list of `if (x != expected) { ok = 0; }` lines, or
calls to a `check(cond, id)` helper (demo46). This is the most repeated
source pattern in the corpus, and a `CHECK` macro makes each line one
statement (see the API below).

### Multiply, divide, modulo

COR24 has `mul` but no divide. tc24r emits `__tc24r_div` and
`__tc24r_mod` routines (25 and 36 call sites; demo4, demo13 and the
`%`-heavy demos). The library provides them as routines, with `DIV`/`MOD`
macros that call them.

### Arrays and pointers

- Element addressing is `base + i*3` for `int` and `base + i` for `char`,
  computed with `shl`/`add` or `mul`.
- Pointer subtraction divides by 3 (demo7).
- Global arrays are `.word`/`.byte` lists or `.space`.
- Multi-dimensional arrays are row-major (demo34).

### Structs and unions

Member access is `base + offset`. Offsets come from the declaration
order: one word per `int` and pointer, one byte per `char`, and arrays
of members are counted in full (demo35). Union members all have offset
0. In hlasm the offsets are `EQU` symbols computed with expressions,
until M6 DSECT/FIELD exists.

### Strings and data

- String literals become `_Sn: .byte ...,0` in `.data`.
- Globals with initialisers become `.word`/`.byte` lists (demo58).
- Adjacent literals are joined (demo63).
- hlasm already turns `.ascii "text\n"` into a `.byte` list with escapes
  resolved, and a macro body can switch to `.data` and back to `.text`.
  That is enough for out-of-line string literals; both were verified
  during this survey.

### Heap

`<stdlib.h>` `malloc` is a bump allocator over a static arena, and `free`
does nothing. demo40, demo43, demo44 and demo45 use it. This maps onto
`GETMAIN`/`FREEMAIN` in the services interface.

### Function pointers

These are `la r0,_fn` stored in a word and called as `jal r1,(r0)`
(demo51-54). They need no macro beyond `CALL` accepting a register or
memory operand as the target.

### Interrupts

demo9 installs an interrupt handler: `la r0,_isr` / `mov iv,r0`, enable
at 0xFF0010, and the handler returns with `jmp (ir)`. hlasm passes these
lines through unchanged, so no macro is needed.

## 2. Macro library API and layout

### COPY member layout

The library lives under `lib/`. A program pulls members in with `COPY`
through its `.sourceset`, and `demos/tinyc/lib.sourceset` lists them
once for all ports:

| Member | Contents | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/cor24.hlasm` | `EQU`s for the board: `UART_DATA`, `UART_STATUS`, `UART_TXBUSY`, `LED_REG`, `INT_ENABLE`, `LED_ON`, `LED_OFF` | symbols only |
| `lib/frame.hlasm` | `PROLOG`, `RET`, `RETURN`, `CALL`, `ARG`, `LOCAL`, `START` | macros only |
| `lib/svc_bare.hlasm` | services interface, bare-metal target: `PUTC`, `PUTS`, `PUTDEC`, `PUTHEX`, `PUTNL`, `WTO`, `GETC`, `GETLINE`, `GETMAIN`, `FREEMAIN`, `EXIT` | macros |
| `lib/svc_bare_rt.hlasm` | the routines those macros call: `_svc_puts`, `_svc_putdec`, `_svc_puthex`, `_svc_getc`, `_svc_getline`, `_svc_getmain` and the arena | code |
| `lib/board.hlasm` | `LEDON`, `LEDOFF`, `BUTTON reg` | macros |
| `lib/rt.hlasm` | runtime routines: `_div`, `_mod`, `_strlen`, `_strcmp`, `_strcpy`, `_memcpy`, `_memset`, `_atoi`, plus `DIV`/`MOD` macros | code and macros |
| `lib/data.hlasm` | `STR label,"text"` (a NUL-terminated string in `.data`), `WORDS label,v1,...`, `BYTES label,v1,...`, `SPACE label,n` | macros |
| `lib/check.hlasm` | `CHECKINIT`, `CHECK cond,a,b`, `CHECKEND 'marker',rc`: the self-test pattern | macros |

Rules:

- **Macros-only members** (`cor24`, `frame`, `svc_bare`, `board`, `data`,
  `check`) can be COPYed at the top of any program, because they emit no
  code until they are called.
- **Code members** (`svc_bare_rt`, `rt`) are COPYed at the end, after the
  program's own routines. Each routine sits inside `IFDEF NEED_<name>`.
  The macros that call a routine `SET NEED_<name>,1`, so only routines
  that were used are emitted. tc24r does the same job with a dead-code
  pass, which demo64 checks. Conditional assembly does it here, which is
  one of the macro features the showcase demonstrates.
- **Each member has an include guard** (`IFNDEF LIB_<member>` /
  `SET LIB_<member>,1`), so a member listed twice is harmless.
- **Library labels** are `_svc_*`, `_rt_*` or the C library name (`_strlen`)
  where a tc24r program would call it. Macro-local labels use `\@`.
- **Choosing the target.** The services interface is the one in
  [limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md#system-services-plan-storage-printing-buffer-io).
  A later `lib/svc_swtos.hlasm` provides the same macros over sw-tos IPC.
  A program chooses its target by which member it COPYs; nothing else
  changes.

### Macro reference (proposed)

Register effects follow the calling convention: macros may clobber r0
and r1 and preserve r2 unless stated.

| Macro | Expands to | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PROLOG [locals]` | `push fp`/`push r2`/`push r1`/`mov fp,sp`; then `add sp,-n` (n ≤ 127) or `sub sp,n` | locals in bytes, default 0 |
| `RET` | `mov sp,fp`/`pop r1`/`pop r2`/`pop fp`/`jmp (r1)` | result already in r0 |
| `RETURN value` | load value into r0, then `RET` | |
| `ARG reg,n` | `lw reg,9+3*(n-1)(fp)` | nth argument (1-based) |
| `LOCAL name,bytes` | `name EQU -offset` from a running `SET` counter; `PROLOG` uses the total | named locals as fp offsets |
| `CALL fn[,a1,...,a8]` | push the arguments right to left (a constant or label with `la r0,`, a register with `push`), `la r0,fn`/`jal r1,(r0)`, then `add sp,3*N` | result in r0 |
| `START [main]` | `_start: la r0,_main`/`jal r1,(r0)`, an optional r0 report, `_halt: bra _halt` | program entry |
| `PUTC [reg]` | wait for TX not busy, `sb reg,0(UART)` (inline, 5 instructions plus `push`/`pop r2`) | default r0 |
| `PUTS label\|reg` | `CALL _svc_puts,arg` | NUL-terminated string |
| `PUTDEC reg`, `PUTHEX reg` | `CALL _svc_putdec`/`_svc_puthex` | signed decimal; 6 hex digits |
| `PUTNL` | `PUTC` of 10 | |
| `WTO "text"` | the string out of line in `.data` (`S\@`), then `PUTS S\@` | escapes resolved by hlasm |
| `GETC reg` | `CALL _svc_getc` | -1 at EOF (0x04) |
| `GETLINE buf,len` | `CALL _svc_getline` | length in r0 |
| `GETMAIN reg,size` / `FREEMAIN reg,size` | bump allocation from the arena / no-op (as tc24r's `free`) | |
| `EXIT [code]` | load code into r0, `bra _halt` | |
| `LEDON` / `LEDOFF` / `BUTTON reg` | `sb` 0/1 to `LED_REG`; `lb reg`, mask bit 0 | |
| `DIV a,b` / `MOD a,b` | `CALL _div,a,b` / `CALL _mod,a,b` | signed, truncating like C |
| `STR label,"text"` | `.data`/`label: .ascii "text"`/`.byte 0`/`.text` | |
| `CHECKINIT` / `CHECK cond,a,b` / `CHECKEND 'DnOK',rc` | clear an ok flag when `cond a,b` is false; at the end print the marker and return rc if all checks passed, else return 0 | the demo self-test |

**Result checking.** The tc24r run scripts check r0 through
`cor24-emu --dump`, but the hlasm e2e harness checks UART output only.
`START` therefore prints `r0=<n>` after `_main` returns when `SET
SHOWRC,1` is in effect, and every port turns it on. A port's expected
output is the C demo's marker followed by `r0=42` (or the demo's own
value), which checks the same two things the tc24r run script does.

## 4. Feature gaps

Cross-checked against
[limits-and-lifting-plan.md](limits-and-lifting-plan.md) (L, D and M
items) and the plsw migration plan (B and G items). Each gap was checked
by running a small program through `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh`.

### Resolved before this plan

These are already done in hlasm, so the library can rely on them:

- **B5/M3: directives inside macro bodies.** Verified: a `CALL` macro
  that pushes 0-3 arguments using `IFEQ &SYSNARG,n`, and pops them with
  `add sp,(&SYSNARG-1)*3`, ran correctly.
- **B6/M2: default parameters.** `PUTC &R=r0` works.
- **Out-of-line data from a macro.** A `WTO` body that switches to `.data`,
  emits `S\@: .ascii "..."`, switches back and calls `_puts` ran correctly,
  with `\n` and `\t` resolved.
- **Large frames.** `sub sp,n` takes a 24-bit immediate, so `PROLOG`
  needs no conditional for frames beyond 127 bytes.

### New gaps that block the library (inserted as step `condition-forms-and-arg-tests`)

| # | Gap | Found | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Structured conditions have no `<=`, `>`, `>=` forms (`cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge`, and unsigned `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`) | most Group B demos; demo46 uses all of them | Without them every C relational operator becomes swapped operands plus an extra register load, or an inverted `IF ... ELSE`. That is exactly the noise the showcase argues macros remove |
| T2 | Conditional assembly cannot classify a macro argument. There is no text comparison (HLASM `AIF ('&A' EQ 'r2')`), and an undefined name in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` silently evaluates to 0, so `IFEQ &A,r2` is true for any argument that is not a symbol | testing `CALL` | `CALL fn,r2,5,_buf` must `push r2` for a register but `la r0,5`/`push r0` for a constant or label. Without a test it needs separate macros per argument kind, which defeats the point of a single `CALL` |

The inserted step adds the six condition forms to IF/ELSEIF/DOEXIT/WHEN,
plus a text test for conditional assembly (for example `IFSAME a,b` /
`IFDIFF a,b`, or quoted-string comparison in `IFEQ`/`IFNE`). It also
decides whether an undefined symbol in `IFEQ`/`IFNE` becomes an ERROR,
checking the existing demos first.

### Known gaps that do not block the ports

| # | Gap | Workaround in the ports | Planned |
|---|---|---|---|
| M5 / G1 | compound conditions (`AND`/`OR`) | nested `IF` (demo11) | plsw-readiness saga |
| M6 / G3 | DSECT/FIELD struct layout | `EQU` offsets with expressions (Group D) | plsw-readiness saga |
| D11 | cor24-asm rejects label arithmetic in `.word` | compute such addresses at run time | assembler issue |
| G7 | assembly time (two passes on the emulator) | none needed at demo size | later cost work |
| — | no `MACRO` definition or `INCLUDE`/`COPY` inside a macro body | not needed by the library | not planned |

Any new gap found during the port steps goes into this table and into
`limits-and-lifting-plan.md`. If it blocks a port, it gets its own saga
step (`agentrail insert`) rather than a workaround.

# The tiny-C demos in hlasm

The C compiler tc24r (`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc`) ships about seventy small
demo programs. This document shows those programs rewritten in hlasm,
side by side with the C, using a shared macro library. The point is to
show what macros buy over writing plain COR24 assembly, and how close
hlasm source can come to the C it replaces.

Status: **planned.** No demo has been ported yet. This page lists the
macros that were chosen and the order of the ports. Each port step adds
its demos below. The detailed survey and reasoning are in
[tinyc-port-plan.md](tinyc-port-plan.md).

## How to run a ported demo

Every port is a source set that COPYs the library members it needs, and
it runs end to end with one command:

```bash
scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh demos/tinyc/hello.sourceset
```

The output is what the program prints on the UART. Like the C demos, each
port prints its `DnOK` marker when its self-checks pass, then `r0=<n>`:
the value `main` returned, which the C demo's run script checks too. Each
port has a regression test named `hlasm_e2e_tinyc_<demo>`.

## The macro library

The library is a set of COPY members under `lib/`. Macros-only members
can be COPYed anywhere, because they produce no code until a macro is
called. Code members (the runtime routines) are COPYed at the end of the
program, and they emit only the routines the program actually called.

The routines follow tc24r's calling convention, so hlasm code and
tc24r-compiled code can call each other:

- arguments are pushed right to left, and the caller pops them;
- the result comes back in r0;
- the prologue is `push fp`/`push r2`/`push r1`, and the first argument is
  at `9(fp)`.

| Member | Macros |
|---|---|
| `lib/cor24.hlasm` | board addresses as `EQU`s: `UART_DATA`, `UART_STATUS`, `LED_REG`, `INT_ENABLE`, `LED_ON`, `LED_OFF` |
| `lib/frame.hlasm` | `PROLOG [locals]`, `RET`, `RETURN value`, `ARG reg,n`, `LOCAL name,bytes`, `CALL fn,args...`, `START` |
| `lib/svc_bare.hlasm` | console and storage: `PUTC`, `PUTS`, `PUTDEC`, `PUTHEX`, `PUTNL`, `WTO "text"`, `GETC`, `GETLINE`, `GETMAIN`, `FREEMAIN`, `EXIT` |
| `lib/board.hlasm` | `LEDON`, `LEDOFF`, `BUTTON reg` |
| `lib/data.hlasm` | `STR label,"text"`, `WORDS`, `BYTES`, `SPACE` |
| `lib/check.hlasm` | `CHECKINIT`, `CHECK cond,a,b`, `CHECKEND 'DnOK',rc`: the demos' self-test pattern |
| `lib/rt.hlasm`, `lib/svc_bare_rt.hlasm` | routines: decimal and hex printing, divide and modulo, `strlen`, `strcmp`, `strcpy`, `memcpy`, `memset`, `atoi`, and the allocator |

`svc_bare.hlasm` is the bare-metal version of the services interface
(console, storage and later buffer I/O). A sw-tos version with the same
macro names can replace it without changing the programs.

To give a feel for the result, this is `hello.c`:

```c
void putc(int c) { while (*(char *)0xFF0101 & 0x80) {} *(char *)0xFF0100 = c; }
void puts(char *s) { while (*s) { putc(*s); s = s + 1; } }
int main() { puts("Hello, COR24!\n"); return 0; }
```

tc24r compiles it to 82 lines of assembly. The planned hlasm port is
about this size:

```
 START
_main:
 PROLOG
 WTO "Hello, COR24!\n"
 RETURN 0
```

## Port plan

Ported demos are added to each group as its step lands.

| Group | Demos |
|---|---|
| A. I/O | uart_tx, hello, led, button, demo2, demo3, demo8, demo10, demo64, demo9 |
| B. Control flow | demo, demo4, demo11, demo12, demo13, demo14, demo15, demo21, demo26, demo46 |
| C. Functions, arrays, pointers, strings | demo5, demo6, demo7, demo16, demo39, demo41, demo50, demo51-54, demo58, demo63 |
| D. Structs, unions, heap | demo23, demo25, demo28, demo34, demo35, demo38, demo40, demo42, demo43 |

The other 26 demos test C syntax that has no assembly counterpart:
typedef, line continuation, prototypes, compound literals, and tc24r
parser regressions. They are not ported. The list and the reasons are
in [tinyc-port-plan.md](tinyc-port-plan.md#demos-to-skip).

## Ported demos

None yet.

content.text:
Step 9, the survey of the tiny-C demos, is done and pushed to `feat/tinyc-macro-ports`. It changed only docs; no hlasm code changed, so I didn't rerun the test suite.

**What I found.** There are 68 C programs; tc24r's generated assembly is checked in for 60 of them. Almost every one is a self-test: it runs some checks, prints `DnOK` on the UART, and returns a known value in r0. Many test C syntax that has no meaning in assembly, such as typedef, line continuation, prototypes and parser bug regressions.

**The plan, in `docs/tinyc-port-plan.md`:**
- **Common patterns.** The one that matters most is UART output: `putc` is called from 522 places. tc24r compiles its 2-line C body into a 25-instruction routine; a macro does it in 7 inline. The plan also covers decimal printing, LED and button, calls and frames, compares, loops, the self-check pattern, divide/modulo, arrays, structs, strings, heap, function pointers and interrupts.
- **Macro library.** Eight members under `lib/`, with macros such as `PROLOG`/`RET`/`CALL`, `PUTC`/`PUTS`/`PUTDEC`/`WTO`, `LEDON`, `STR`, `GETMAIN` and `CHECK`.
  - They follow tc24r's calling convention, so library code and tc24r-compiled code can call each other. The PL/SW migration plan needs this.
  - Runtime routines are emitted only if the program uses them.
  - Ports print `r0=<n>` at the end, so the end-to-end test checks both the marker and the return value, the same two things the C run scripts check.
- **Ports.** 42 demos in four groups: I/O, control flow, functions/arrays/strings, and structs/heap. The other 26 are skipped, each with a reason. The two large Lisp demos (44 and 45) are optional extras for the showcase.
- **Gaps.** I tried the key macro designs through the new harness. `CALL` with a variable number of arguments, out-of-line strings with escapes, and large stack frames already work.

`docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md` is started as the user-facing page: the chosen macros, the port order, and `hello.c` next to what its port should look like (about 5 lines, versus 96 lines of tc24r output).

**Two new gaps block the library, so I inserted a step for them** (now step 10, before the library):
- **M8:** IF/DO conditions have no `<=`, `>`, `>=` forms, signed or unsigned. Every C comparison would need swapped operands or an inverted IF, and demo46 uses all of them.
- **M9:** a macro can't tell whether an argument is a register. Worse, an undefined name in `IFEQ` quietly counts as 0, so `IFEQ &A,r2` is true for almost any argument. One `CALL` macro can't push `r2` directly and load a constant with `la`.

I also split the function/data port step in two (step 15 now does structs/unions/heap), because together they were 22 demos. The saga now has 16 steps; the showcase is last.

**Next** is step 10, adding the M8 condition forms and the M9 argument test to hlasm. I'll start it when you say go.

; Demo 43: condition forms and argument tests. Every structured compare
; (cc_eq ... cc_geu) runs on the pairs (1,2) (2,2) (3,2) (-1,1) and prints T
; or F for each, first with a register right-hand side, then with a
; constant; -1 against 1 shows signed versus unsigned. A DOEXIT and an
; ELSEIF use the new forms too. Then PUSHARG, a CALL-style macro, uses
; IFSAME to push a register argument directly and load anything else with
; la. Assembled and run on cor24-emu this prints (see hlasm_e2e_d43):
;   eq FTFF ne TFTT lt TFFT le TTFT gt FFTF ge FTTF
;   lu TFFF leu TTFF gtu FFTT geu FTTT
; twice, then "loop 5 mid 7 sum 42".
UART EQU -65280

; PUTC: print the character in r0
MACRO PUTC
 push r2
 la r2,UART
L\@:
 lb r1,1(r2)
 cls r1,z
 brt L\@
 sb r0,0(r2)
 pop r2
MEND

; PUTS2: print two or three characters and a blank
MACRO PUTS2 &A,&B,&C
 lc r0,&A
 PUTC
 lc r0,&B
 PUTC
IFDIFF &C,
 lc r0,&C
 PUTC
ENDIFASM
 lc r0,' '
 PUTC
MEND

; TR: print T if "&CC r0,r1" holds for r0=&A, r1=&B, else F
MACRO TR &CC,&A,&B
 lc r0,&A
 lc r1,&B
IF &CC,r0,r1
 lc r0,'T'
ELSE
 lc r0,'F'
ENDIF
 PUTC
MEND

; TK: the same with the constant &B as the right-hand side
MACRO TK &CC,&A,&B
 lc r0,&A
IF &CC,r0,&B
 lc r0,'T'
ELSE
 lc r0,'F'
ENDIF
 PUTC
MEND

; FORM: one condition over the four pairs, using test macro &T
MACRO FORM &T,&CC,&N1,&N2,&N3
 PUTS2 &N1,&N2,&N3
 &T &CC,1,2
 &T &CC,2,2
 &T &CC,3,2
 &T &CC,-1,1
 lc r0,' '
 PUTC
MEND

; ALL: every condition with test macro &T, on two lines
MACRO ALL &T
 FORM &T,cc_eq,'e','q'
 FORM &T,cc_ne,'n','e'
 FORM &T,cc_lt,'l','t'
 FORM &T,cc_le,'l','e'
 FORM &T,cc_gt,'g','t'
 FORM &T,cc_ge,'g','e'
 lc r0,10
 PUTC
 FORM &T,cc_lu,'l','u'
 FORM &T,cc_leu,'l','e','u'
 FORM &T,cc_gtu,'g','t','u'
 FORM &T,cc_geu,'g','e','u'
 lc r0,10
 PUTC
MEND

; PUTDIG: print r0 (0-99) in decimal
MACRO PUTDIG
 lc r1,0
DO
 DOEXIT cc_lt,r0,10
 add r0,-10
 add r1,1
ENDDO
 push r0
IF cc_gt,r1,0
 lc r0,'0'
 add r0,r1
 PUTC
ENDIF
 pop r0
 add r0,'0'
 PUTC
MEND

; PUSHARG: push a call argument -- a register as it is, anything else
; (a constant or a label) through la r0
MACRO PUSHARG &A
IFSAME &A,r0
 push r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r1
 push r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r2
 push r2
ELSEASM
 la r0,&A
 push r0
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND

; CALL2: call &F with two arguments, pushed right to left
MACRO CALL2 &F,&A,&B
 PUSHARG &B
 PUSHARG &A
 la r0,&F
 jal r1,(r0)
 add sp,6
MEND

_start:
 ALL TR
 ALL TK

; DOEXIT with cc_ge: count up until r0 >= 5
 PUTS2 'l','o','o'
 lc r0,0
DO
 DOEXIT cc_ge,r0,5
 add r0,1
ENDDO
 PUTDIG
 lc r0,' '
 PUTC

; ELSEIF with cc_le and cc_gtu: classify 7
 PUTS2 'm','i','d'
 lc r2,7
IF cc_le,r2,3
 lc r0,1
ELSEIF cc_gtu,r2,9
 lc r0,9
ELSE
 mov r0,r2
ENDIF
 PUTDIG
 lc r0,' '
 PUTC

; CALL2 with a register, a constant and a label argument
 PUTS2 's','u','m'
 lc r2,30
 CALL2 _add2,r2,_ten
 mov r2,r0
 CALL2 _add2,r2,2
 PUTDIG
 lc r0,10
 PUTC
halt:
 bra halt

; _add2(a, b): a + b, where b below 64 is a value and above it an address
; of a word holding the value
_add2:
 push fp
 push r2
 push r1
 mov fp,sp
 lw r0,9(fp)
 lw r1,12(fp)
IF cc_geu,r1,64
 lw r1,0(r1)
ENDIF
 add r0,r1
 mov sp,fp
 pop r1
 pop r2
 pop fp
 jmp (r1)

_ten:
 .word 10

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_expr_errors.sh -- expression and string-escape errors stop with ERROR.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/hlasm-expr.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# run <label> <source text>: run hlasm and print its ERROR line (or "ok").
run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$2" > "$WORK/$1.hlasm"
    bash demos/make_bin.sh "$WORK/$1.hlasm" "$WORK/$1.bin" >/dev/null
    scripts/run-kernel.sh hlasm.s --load-binary "$WORK/$1.bin@524288" \
        --speed 0 -n 400000 -q > "$WORK/$1.out" 2>&1 || true
    if grep -q '^ERROR:' "$WORK/$1.out"; then
        printf '%s: %s\n' "$1" "$(grep -m1 '^ERROR:' "$WORK/$1.out" | tr -d '\r')"
    else
        printf '%s: ok: %s\n' "$1" "$(tr -d '\r' < "$WORK/$1.out" | grep -v '^Executed' | grep . | tail -1)"
    fi
}

run div_zero 'X EQU 1/0'
run mod_zero 'X EQU 7%(2-2)'
run str_bad_escape '.ascii "a\q"'
run str_bad_hex '.ascii "\xZ1"'
run char_bad_escape ' lc r0,'"'"'\q'"'"''
run str_good '.asciz "\x41\\\"\t"'
run char_good ' lc r0,'"'"'\n'"'"'+1'
check_expr_errors.sh

## Conditional assembly

Conditional assembly includes or skips source lines at assembly time:

```
SET DEBUG,1
SET LEVEL,2
IFDEF DEBUG
 nop
ENDIFASM
IFEQ LEVEL,3
 add r0,3
ELSEASM
 add r0,1
ENDIFASM
IFNDEF RELEASE
 lc r1,0
ENDIFASM
```

Output:

```
 nop
 add r0,1
 lc r1,0
```

| Directive | Includes the block when |
|---|---|
| `IFDEF name` | the symbol is defined and not 0 |
| `IFNDEF name` | the symbol is not defined |
| `IFEQ expr,expr` | the two values are equal (an undefined symbol counts as 0) |
| `IFNE expr,expr` | the two values differ |
| `ELSEASM` | the preceding condition was false |
| `ENDIFASM` | ends the block |

Blocks nest up to 32 deep. Everything inside a skipped block is skipped,
including nested blocks whose own condition is true.

## Structured control flow

Structured statements compare a register with a value and generate the
labels and branches. Conditions are written `cc, register, value`:

| Condition | True when |
|---|---|
| `cc_eq` | register = value |
| `cc_ne` | register != value |
| `cc_lt` | register < value (signed) |
| `cc_lu` | register < value (unsigned) |
| `cc_zset` | the C flag is set (no operands; test a compare you just did) |
| `cc_zclr` | the C flag is clear |

The value can be a register, a number, or a symbol expression. A constant is
loaded into a scratch register that is saved and restored around the
compare (`push r2` / `lc r2,...` / `pop r2`), so the generated code changes
no registers except the ones your own code changes.

### IF / ELSEIF / ELSE / ENDIF

```
LIMIT EQU 10
IF cc_lt, r0, LIMIT
 add r0,1
ELSE
 lc r0,0
ENDIF
```

Output:

```
 push r2

## Limits and error messages

hlasm checks every limit. Exceeding one stops hlasm with a single `ERROR:`
line; nothing is silently truncated.

| Item | Limit | Error |
|---|---|---|
| Source line | 256 characters | `input line longer than 256 characters` |
| Symbols | 512 | `symbol table overflow (512 symbols)` |
| Symbol name | 31 characters | `symbol name longer than 31 characters` |
| Macros | 256 | `macro table overflow (256 macros)` |
| Macro name | 31 characters | `macro name longer than 31 characters` |
| Macro parameters | 16 | `more than 16 macro parameters` |
| Parameter name | 31 characters | `macro parameter name longer than 31 characters` |
| All macro bodies | 64 KB | `macro body pool overflow (65536 bytes)` |
| Expanded macro line | 256 characters | `expanded macro line longer than 256 characters` |
| Macro call nesting | 8 | `macro calls nested deeper than 8` |
| Macro arguments | 16 | `more than 16 macro arguments` |
| Parameter default | 63 characters | `macro parameter default longer than 63 characters` |
| Conditional nesting | 32 | `conditional assembly nested deeper than 32` |
| IF / DO / SELECT nesting | 32 each | `IF nested deeper than 32` (and DO, SELECT) |
| Division | non-zero divisor | `division by zero in expression` |
| String escapes | see above | `unknown escape in string or character literal` |
| Source set members | 32 | `source config has more than 32 members` (`make_cfg.sh` also refuses) |
| Member name | 15 characters | refused by `make_cfg.sh` |
| INCLUDE / COPY nesting | 16 | `INCLUDE nested deeper than 16` |

Each message is preceded by the member and line (see "Multiple source files"). For
example, `SET THIS_NAME_IS_MUCH_TOO_LONG_FOR_HLASM,1` on line 2 of a source
run without a source set gives:

```
ERROR: main:2: symbol name longer than 31 characters
```

Values are 24-bit and wrap like COR24 arithmetic. Structured labels and
`\@` numbers have no practical limit.

## Not supported yet

These are planned (see `docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md` for the schedule):

- **Compound conditions** (`IF cc_eq,r0,1,AND,...`) and record layouts
  (`DSECT`).
- **Labels as values.** Labels are resolved by `cor24-asm`, not hlasm, so
  they cannot be used in `EQU`, `SET` or conditions.

## Further reading

- `demos/README.md`: the demo programs (d01-d41) and what each shows.

input.old_string:
| `IFEQ expr,expr` | the two values are equal (an undefined symbol counts as 0) |
| `IFNE expr,expr` | the two values differ |
| `ELSEASM` | the preceding condition was false |
| `ENDIFASM` | ends the block |

Blocks nest up to 32 deep. Everything inside a skipped block is skipped,
including nested blocks whose own condition is true.
input.new_string:
| `IFEQ expr,expr` | the two values are equal |
| `IFNE expr,expr` | the two values differ |
| `IFSAME a,b` | the two operands are the same text |
| `IFDIFF a,b` | the two operands are different text |
| `ELSEASM` | the preceding condition was false |
| `ENDIFASM` | ends the block |

Blocks nest up to 32 deep. Everything inside a skipped block is skipped,
including nested blocks whose own condition is true.

The first operand of `IFEQ`/`IFNE` is an expression of numbers and
`SET`/`EQU` symbols. Any other name (a typo, a label, a register) stops
hlasm with `IFEQ/IFNE operand is not a SET or EQU symbol`, except inside a
skipped block, so `IFDEF X` / `IFEQ X,1` is safe when X is not defined.

`IFSAME`/`IFDIFF` compare text, which is how a macro tells what kind of
argument it was given. The comparison is exact (case matters, `R2` is not
`r2`) and happens after argument substitution. An operand ends at a comma,
blank, tab or `;` outside quotes and parentheses, and either operand may be
empty, so `IFDIFF &C,` tests whether `&C` was passed. From demo d43:

```
; PUSHARG: push a call argument -- a register as it is, anything else
; (a constant or a label) through la r0
MACRO PUSHARG &A
IFSAME &A,r0
 push r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r1
 push r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r2
 push r2
ELSEASM
 la r0,&A
 push r0
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND
```

| `cc_le` | register <= value (signed) |
| `cc_gt` | register > value (signed) |

| `cc_zset` | the C flag is set (no operands; test a compare you just did) |

Any other name stops hlasm with `unknown structured condition`. COR24 only
compares "less than", so `cc_gt` and `cc_le` compare with the operands
swapped (`cls value,register`), and `cc_ge` and `cc_le` branch on the
opposite result.

The value can be a register, a number, or a symbol expression.

# HLASM Macro-Assembler Demos

Each demo is a self-contained `.hlasm` source file showing one or more features.
Use `make_bin.sh` to convert `.hlasm` to `.bin` for loading into the emulator.

## Feature Status

| Demo | Feature | Status |
|------|---------|--------|
| d01 | Basic passthrough | WORKS |
| d02 | Simple macro (no params) | WORKS |
| d03 | HLASM-style named macro parameters | WORKS |
| d04 | SET / IFDEF / ENDIFASM | WORKS |
| d05 | IFEQ / IFNE comparison | WORKS |
| d06 | ELSEASM toggle | WORKS |
| d07 | Nested conditionals | WORKS |
| d08 | Macros + conditionals | WORKS |
| d09 | Comments (; and #) | WORKS (pass through) |
| d10 | Multiple macros | WORKS |
| d11 | IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF | WORKS |
| d12 | DO/DOEXIT/ENDDO loops | WORKS |
| d13 | SELECT/WHEN/ENDSEL | WORKS |
| d14 | IFNDEF (not defined) | WORKS |
| d15 | Realistic program | WORKS |
| d16 | Bootstrap `hlasm0` subset | WORKS |
| d17 | Multi-buffer source input | WORKS |
| d18 | Include-ready multi-buffer chain | WORKS |
| d19 | Bootstrap memory map proof | WORKS |
| d20 | Patchable main source window | WORKS |
| d21 | Directive-driven source switch | WORKS |
| d22 | Include-return source stack | WORKS |
| d23 | Named include table | WORKS |
| d24 | Nested named includes | WORKS |
| d25 | Split bootstrap sourceset proof | WORKS |
| d26 | Structured branch-range hardening | WORKS |
| d27 | Positional macro parameters | WORKS |
| d28 | Macro robustness stress | WORKS |
| d29 | Control-flow integration proof | WORKS |
| d30 | Structured annotation comments | WORKS |
| d31 | Large source + macro capacity | WORKS |
| d32 | Literals and data ergonomics | WORKS |
| d33 | Symbols and expressions | WORKS |
| d34 | COPY macro library workflow | WORKS |
| d35 | Listing/xref comments | WORKS |
| d36 | End-of-run HLXREF report | WORKS |
| d36 | IF/ELSEIF/ENDIF without ELSE | WORKS |
| d37 | HLDIAG diagnostic baseline | WORKS |
| d38 | HLDIAG unknown mnemonic | WORKS |
| d39 | HLDIAG undefined symbol | WORKS |
| d40 | Long-range structured jumps (far form + trampoline) | WORKS |
| d41 | EQU constants, expressions, symbols in operands (prints CA4Y2! when run) | WORKS |
| d42 | Macro layering: nested/recursive calls, directives and IF in bodies, default/keyword params, &SYSNARG (prints Hi!***-7Vok. when run) | WORKS |

## Demo Policy

Every new HLASM feature or bootstrap milestone should add:

- one source demo
- one `reg-rs` regression test
- one README status entry

## Running a Demo

```bash
# Convert source to binary
bash demos/make_bin.sh demos/d01_passthrough.hlasm demos/d01_passthrough.bin

# Run on emulator
scripts/run-kernel.sh hlasm.s --load-binary demos/d01_passthrough.bin@524288 --speed 0 -n 100000 2>&1
```

## HLASM Syntax Reference

### Macros

Current supported baseline:

- `MACRO name` starts a definition and `MEND` ends it
- definition lines are consumed by the assembler and are not emitted to output
- simple no-parameter invocations expand stably
- positional parameters `&1`, `&2`, ... expand stably
- HLASM-style named parameters `&name` in both the definition header and body
  expand stably
- macro names up to 31 characters are supported
- `&NAME=default` header parameters and `NAME=value` keyword arguments
- expanded lines go back through the line processor, so bodies may call
  macros (8 deep), and use conditional assembly and structured statements;
  `&SYSNARG` is the positional argument count (demo d42)

```
MACRO name
 <body>
MEND
<name>              ; invoke macro
```

This repo is aiming toward HLASM-like behavior on the MVS lineage, but the
currently implemented macro subset is still narrower than full HLASM macro
semantics.

Named parameters:
```
MACRO PUSH2 &LEFT,&RIGHT
 push &LEFT
 push &RIGHT
MEND
PUSH2 r0,r1
```

Positional parameters:
```
MACRO PUSH2
 push &1
 push &2
MEND
PUSH2 r0,r1
```

### Conditional Assembly (SET / IFDEF / IFNDEF / IFEQ / IFNE / ELSEASM / ENDIFASM)

```
SET DEBUG,1         ; define symbol DEBUG = 1

IFDEF DEBUG         ; include if DEBUG is defined
 nop
ENDIFASM

IFNDEF RELEASE      ; include if RELEASE is NOT defined
 nop
ENDIFASM

IFEQ VER,3          ; include if VER equals 3
 nop
ELSEASM             ; otherwise include this block
 add r0,1
ENDIFASM

IFNE VER,2          ; include if VER does NOT equal 2
 sub r0,1
ENDIFASM
```

Assembly-time numeric literals accepted by `SET`, `IFEQ`, `IFNE`, and
structured compare lowering:
```
SET COUNT,42
SET MASK,0x2A
SET BITS,0b101010
SET SAME,2Ah
```

Assembly-time expressions (`| ^ & << >> + - * / %`, unary `- ~`, parentheses,
character literals; see docs/user-guide.md) work in `SET`, `EQU`,
`IFEQ`, `IFNE`, structured compares, and instruction/.byte/.word operands,
where symbol expressions are replaced by their decimal values (demo d41):
```
MASK EQU 0x20
STEP EQU 2
SET BASE,8
SET TOTL,MASK+BASE+STEP
IFEQ TOTL,42
 nop
ENDIFASM
```

Current-location and label arithmetic remain assembler passthrough, not
assembly-time evaluation inside `hlasm`:
```
mark:
 .word mark+3
 .word tail-mark
tail:
```

### Data Directives

Current practical data-directive conveniences:

- `.ascii "text"` lowers to a `.byte` list
- `.asciz "text"` lowers to a `.byte` list with trailing `0`
- `.space N` lowers to `N` zero bytes
- `.fill N,V` lowers to `N` copies of byte value `V`

Examples:
```
.ascii "HI\n"
.asciz "OK"
.space 4
.fill 3,0x7F
```

### Source Buffer Control

```
SRCBUF 1            ; jump directly to preloaded source slot 1

INCBUF 1            ; push current slot/position, read slot 1, then
                    ; return to the caller source when slot 1 hits EOF

INCLUDE tail        ; resolve "tail" through the member names in the config block,
                    ; then include that slot and resume the caller source

COPY libmac         ; HLASM-style alias for a named source member, useful
                    ; for macro and symbol library fragments
```

Bootstrap-facing include demos and proofs now use a source-set manifest:
optional `PROFILE file`, then `ROOT dir`, optional `MAINADDR` / `EXTRAADDR` /
`ALIGN`, `SOURCESET child.sourceset`, then `MAIN file.hlasm` plus repeated
`INCLUDE name file.hlasm` or `COPY name file.hlasm`. The host-side runner
builds the `.bin` files, packs include buffers from their real sizes, emits the
unchanged low-SRAM config image, and feeds the same runtime include table into
`hlasm.s`.

Demo 34 uses the same composed source-set path to package a small copied macro
library plus a copied symbol library, then consumes both from a main source via
`COPY`.

Demo 24 now uses that composed source-set path directly, so the fragment model
is exercised on a named-include proof as well as the split `hlasm0` bootstrap
proof.

Demo 23 now uses the same composed source-set path, so both named-include
proofs run through the shared demo profile and fragment workflow.

Conditionals can nest:
```
SET OUTER,1
SET INNER,0
IFDEF OUTER
 IFDEF INNER
  add r0,1
 ELSEASM
  nop
 ENDIFASM
ELSEASM
 sub r0,1
ENDIFASM
```

### Structured Control Flow

#### IF / ELSEIF / ELSE / ENDIF
Nested `IF` blocks and `ELSEIF` chains now lower to plain labels and branches.
Structured conditionals are emitted in a long-range-safe form: a short
reversed conditional branch skips over an unconditional transfer, so generated
control flow does not depend on raw `bra` reach. The transfer is `bra L`
when its worst-case offset fits; otherwise it is `push r2` / `la r2,L_far` /
`jmp (r2)`, and the target gets a `bra L` / `L_far:` / `pop r2` trampoline
(see docs/structured-jump-relaxation.md; hlasm sizes its output in a first
pass to decide).
When `SET HLANN,1` is active, `hlasm` also emits opt-in semicolon comment
lines that mark structured source boundaries in the lowered `.s` output.

When `SET HLIST,1` is active, `hlasm` emits broader listing/xref-friendly
semicolon comments for consumed source-level events such as:

- `COPY name`
- `MACRO name`
- `EXPAND name`
- `EQU name`

`HLIST` is intended for understanding generated assembly and expansion flow.
`HLANN` remains the narrower switch for structured-control-flow source markers.
They can be used independently.
`HLXREF` is a separate opt-in switch for a compact end-of-run cross-reference
section.

When `SET HLXREF,1` is active, `hlasm` emits a compact end-of-run section:

```asm
; HLASM XREF BEGIN
; HLASM XREF COPY libmac
; HLASM XREF MACRO PUSH2
; HLASM XREF EXPAND PUSH2 1
; HLASM XREF SYMBOL LOCAL
; HLASM XREF END
```

```
IF cc_eq, r0, 0
    add r1,1
    IF cc_ne, r1, z
        lc r0,0
    ELSEIF cc_lt, r2, 10
        add r2,1
    ELSE
        nop
    ENDIF
ELSEIF cc_zclr
    add r0,1
ELSE
    add r2,2
ENDIF
```
Condition codes: cc_eq, cc_ne, cc_lt (signed), cc_lu (unsigned),
cc_zset (C flag set), cc_zclr (C flag clear).

Annotation example:
```
SET HLANN,1
IF cc_eq, r0, 0
    add r1,1
ENDIF
```

This emits normal lowered assembly plus comment markers such as:
```
; HLASM IF cc_eq, r0, 0
; HLASM THEN
; HLASM ENDIF
```

#### DO / DOEXIT / ITERATE / ENDDO
Loop lowering uses the same long-range-safe pattern for generated exits and
back-edges, with unconditional structured transfers relaxed the same way.

```
DO
    add r0,1
    DOEXIT cc_eq, r0, 10
    nop
ENDDO
DO
    add r1,1
    ITERATE
ENDDO
```

#### SELECT / WHEN / OTHERWISE / ENDSEL
```
SELECT r0
    WHEN 0
        add r1,1
    WHEN 1
        add r2,1
    OTHERWISE
        lc r1,0
ENDSEL
```

### Passthrough

Any line that is not a directive, macro definition, or structured keyword
is emitted unchanged. This includes labels, instructions, and comment lines.

### Labels
```
mylabel:
 bra mylabel
```

content.text:
Step 10 is done, so both gaps the survey found are fixed in hlasm. All 79 tests pass, and the work is committed and pushed to `feat/tinyc-macro-ports`.

**M8, the missing comparisons.** IF, ELSEIF and DOEXIT now accept `cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge` and the unsigned `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`, against either a register or a constant.
- COR24 can only test "less than". So `gt` and `le` compare with the operands swapped, and `ge` and `le` branch on the opposite result. One small table drives this, and the old chains of name checks are gone.
- There's no `cls z,r0` instruction, so a swapped compare against `z` uses the constant 0 instead.
- An unknown condition name such as `cc_foo` now stops with an `ERROR:`. Before, it silently became an unsigned less-than.
- WHEN is unchanged; it still tests for equality with the SELECT value.

**M9, telling what kind of argument a macro got.** There are two new directives, `IFSAME a,b` and `IFDIFF a,b`.
- They compare the text of the two operands exactly, so `R2` is not `r2`. Either operand may be empty, so `IFDIFF &C,` tests whether `&C` was passed.
- The library's `CALL` can now `push r2` for a register argument and use `la` for a constant or label.
- `IFEQ`/`IFNE` now stop with an `ERROR:` when the first operand isn't a SET/EQU symbol. Before, such a name silently counted as 0. No existing demo depended on the old behavior. Inside a block that is already being skipped there's no error, so `IFDEF X` followed by `IFEQ X,1` still works when X is undefined.

**Tests**
- **Demo d43**, run end to end by `hlasm_e2e_d43_condition_forms`:
  - prints T/F for every condition, with register and with constant operands, over pairs that include -1 vs 1 (signed and unsigned give different answers there);
  - exercises DOEXIT and ELSEIF with the new forms;
  - calls a CALL-style macro with a register, a constant and a label argument.

  The program's output matched the expected table on the first run.
- **`reg-rs/check_conditions.sh`**: the new errors and the IFSAME/IFDIFF edge cases (empty operands, quoted text containing commas, case, blanks around operands).

**Side effects on existing tests**
- Two extra directive checks per line make hlasm slightly slower, so 50 expected outputs changed only in their instruction counts. I compared the program output of each before updating them; only d19, which dumps hlasm's own memory image, differed.
- The d25 test uses a fixed 460K instruction budget that now runs out just before the end. I raised it to 1M, the same limit `./build.sh bootstrap` got in step 7.
- d43 needs about 37M hlasm instructions because its macros expand to about 2,800 lines. Its test sets a 60M budget; it runs in under a second.

The user guide, demos README, limits plan and port plan are updated.

**Next** is step 11: build the macro library under `lib/` (frames and calls, console output, LED/button, data, self-checks) with an end-to-end test for each macro. I'll start it when you say go.

; lib/frame.hlasm -- routine frames and calls (macros only, no code).
;
; The calling convention is tc24r's, so these routines and tc24r-compiled
; ones can call each other:
;   caller: push the arguments right to left (one word each), jal, and pop
;           them; the result comes back in r0
;   callee: push fp, r2, r1; mov fp,sp; locals below fp; the first argument
;           is at 9(fp), the second at 12(fp), ...
; r0 and r1 are scratch across a call; r2 and fp are preserved.
;
; A routine looks like this:
;   _sum3:
;    LOCAL TMP,3          ; optional: name a 3-byte local (TMP = -3)
;    PROLOG               ; frame; reserves the LOCAL bytes
;    ARG r0,1             ; r0 = first argument
;    ARG r1,2
;    add r0,r1
;    sw r0,TMP(fp)
;    ...
;    RET                  ; result in r0
IFNDEF LIB_FRAME
SET LIB_FRAME,1
; bytes of LOCALs declared since the last PROLOG
SET LOCSZ,0

; LOADR reg,value -- reg = value, where value is a register (mov, or nothing
; if it is reg itself), or a constant, character or label (la).
MACRO LOADR &R,&V
IFDIFF &R,&V
IFSAME &V,r0
 mov &R,r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &V,r1
 mov &R,r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &V,r2
 mov &R,r2
ELSEASM
 la &R,&V
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND

; PUSHARG value -- push one call argument: a register as it is; a constant,
; character or label through r1 (so r1 is clobbered).
MACRO PUSHARG &A
IFSAME &A,r0
 push r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r1
 push r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r2
 push r2
ELSEASM
 la r1,&A
 push r1
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND

; CALL fn[,a1,...,a8] -- call fn with up to 8 arguments, pushed right to left
; and popped after the call; the result is in r0. fn is a label, or r0 or
; r2 holding a routine address. Constant and label arguments are loaded
; through r1, so an r1 argument must have only register arguments to its
; right; r0 and r2 arguments are always safe.
MACRO CALL &F,&A1,&A2,&A3,&A4,&A5,&A6,&A7,&A8
IFDIFF &A8,
 PUSHARG &A8
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A7,
 PUSHARG &A7
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A6,
 PUSHARG &A6
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A5,
 PUSHARG &A5
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A4,
 PUSHARG &A4
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A3,
 PUSHARG &A3
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A2,
 PUSHARG &A2
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &A1,
 PUSHARG &A1
ENDIFASM
IFSAME &F,r2
 jal r1,(r2)
ELSEASM
IFDIFF &F,r0
 la r0,&F
ENDIFASM
 jal r1,(r0)
ENDIFASM
IFNE &SYSNARG,1
 add sp,(&SYSNARG-1)*3
ENDIFASM
MEND

; LOCAL name,bytes -- name a local of the given size; name becomes its
; (negative) offset from fp. Declare locals before PROLOG. Offsets below
; -128 do not fit lw/sw; address such locals with mov/add instead.
MACRO LOCAL &N,&B
SET LOCSZ,LOCSZ+&B
SET &N,0-LOCSZ
MEND

; PROLOG [bytes] -- routine entry: save fp, r2, r1, set fp, and reserve
; bytes of locals (default: the LOCALs declared since the last PROLOG).
MACRO PROLOG &B
 push fp
 push r2
 push r1
 mov fp,sp
IFDIFF &B,
 sub sp,&B
ELSEASM
IFNE LOCSZ,0
 sub sp,LOCSZ
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
SET LOCSZ,0
MEND

; RET -- routine exit: restore sp, r1, r2, fp and return (result in r0).
MACRO RET
 mov sp,fp
 pop r1
 pop r2
 pop fp
 jmp (r1)
MEND

; RETURN value -- r0 = value (register, constant or label), then RET.
MACRO RETURN &V
 LOADR r0,&V
 RET
MEND

; ARG reg,n -- reg = the nth argument (1-based) of the current routine.
MACRO ARG &R,&N
 lw &R,6+3*&N(fp)
MEND
ENDIFASM

input.content:
; lib/svc_bare.hlasm -- system services interface, bare-metal target
; (macros only). The routines these macros call are in svc_bare_code, which
; the program COPYs at its end; a routine is emitted only if a macro here
; asked for it (SET NEED_<name>,1). A sw-tos target can provide the same
; macros on top of IPC without changing the programs.
; Needs: cor24, frame.
;
; Register effects: every macro may clobber r0 and r1 and preserves r2 and
; fp, unless its description says otherwise.
IFNDEF LIB_SVC
SET LIB_SVC,1

; START [main] -- program entry: .text, _start calls main (default _main),
; then falls into _exit. Put it before any other code.
MACRO START &M=_main
 .text
_start:
 la r0,&M
 jal r1,(r0)
 EXITCODE
MEND

; EXITCODE -- the program's exit path (used by START): _exit, then with
; SET SHOWRC,1 print "r0=<n>" and a newline (n is r0, the exit code),
; then halt (bra to itself, which cor24-emu treats as a stop).
MACRO EXITCODE
_exit:
IFDEF SHOWRC
 push r0
 lc r0,114
 PUTC
 lc r0,48
 PUTC
 lc r0,61
 PUTC
 lw r0,0(sp)
 PUTDEC
 PUTNL
 pop r0
ENDIFASM
_halt:
 bra _halt
MEND

; EXIT [code] -- stop the program from anywhere: r0 = code (register,
; constant or label; default: r0 as it is), then jump to _exit.
MACRO EXIT &C=r0
 LOADR r0,&C
 la r1,_exit
 jmp (r1)
MEND

; PUTC [char] -- write one character to the UART, waiting while the
; transmitter is busy. char is a register (default r0), a constant or a
; character such as 'A'. Inline; clobbers r0 and r1.
MACRO PUTC &C=r0
 LOADR r0,&C
 push r2
 la r2,UART_DATA
L\@:
 lb r1,1(r2)
 cls r1,z
 brt L\@
 sb r0,0(r2)
 pop r2
MEND

; PUTNL -- write a newline (10).
MACRO PUTNL
 PUTC 10
MEND

; PUTS str -- write the NUL-terminated string at str (a label or a register
; holding its address). No newline is added.
MACRO PUTS &S
SET NEED_svc_puts,1
 CALL _svc_puts,&S
MEND

; PUTDEC [reg] -- write a value in signed decimal (default r0); a
; register, constant or label.
MACRO PUTDEC &V=r0
SET NEED_svc_putdec,1
 CALL _svc_putdec,&V
MEND

; PUTHEX [reg] -- write a value in lower-case hex without leading zeros
; (as tc24r's printf %x).
MACRO PUTHEX &V=r0
SET NEED_svc_puthex,1
 CALL _svc_puthex,&V
MEND

; WTO "text" -- write a literal string. The text is stored out of line in
; .data (escapes such as \n are resolved by hlasm).
MACRO WTO &T
 .data
WTO\@:
 .ascii &T
 .byte 0
 .text
 PUTS WTO\@
MEND

; GETC [reg] -- wait for a character from the UART and return it in r0
; (and reg, if given and not r0).
MACRO GETC &R=r0
SET NEED_svc_getc,1

; lib/svc_bare_code.hlasm -- routines behind the svc_bare macros. COPY it

IFNDEF LIB_SVC_CODE
SET LIB_SVC_CODE,1

; _svc_getline(buf, len): read a line; see GETLINE. Placed before _svc_getc,
; which it uses.
IFDEF NEED_svc_getline
_svc_getline:
 LOCAL GL_N,3
 PROLOG
 ARG r2,1
 lc r0,0
 sw r0,GL_N(fp)
DO
 lw r0,GL_N(fp)
 ARG r1,2
 add r1,-1
 DOEXIT cc_ge,r0,r1
 GETC
 DOEXIT cc_eq,r0,10
 sb r0,0(r2)
 add r2,1
 lw r0,GL_N(fp)
 add r0,1
 sw r0,GL_N(fp)
ENDDO
 lc r0,0
 sb r0,0(r2)
 lw r0,GL_N(fp)
 RET
ENDIFASM

; _svc_getc(): wait for UART RX ready, return the character (0-255).
IFDEF NEED_svc_getc
_svc_getc:
 PROLOG
 la r2,UART_DATA
DO
 lbu r0,1(r2)
 lc r1,UART_RXREADY
 and r0,r1
 DOEXIT cc_ne,r0,0
ENDDO
 lbu r0,0(r2)
 RET
ENDIFASM

; _svc_puts(str): write a NUL-terminated string.
IFDEF NEED_svc_puts
_svc_puts:
 PROLOG
 ARG r2,1
DO
 lbu r0,0(r2)
 DOEXIT cc_eq,r0,0
 PUTC
 add r2,1
ENDDO
 RET
ENDIFASM

; _svc_putdec(n): write n in signed decimal. The magnitude is handled as
; unsigned, so -8388608 prints correctly.
IFDEF NEED_svc_putdec
_svc_putdec:
 LOCAL PD_P,3
 LOCAL PD_S,3
 PROLOG
 lc r0,0
 sw r0,PD_S(fp)
 ARG r2,1
IF cc_lt,r2,0
 PUTC '-'
 lc r0,0
 sub r0,r2
 mov r2,r0
ENDIF
 la r0,_svc_pow10
 sw r0,PD_P(fp)
; one digit per power of ten above 1: count subtractions; skip leading 0s
DO
 lw r1,PD_P(fp)
 lw r1,0(r1)
 DOEXIT cc_eq,r1,1
 lc r0,0
DO
 DOEXIT cc_lu,r2,r1
 sub r2,r1
 add r0,1
ENDDO
IF cc_eq,r0,0
 lw r1,PD_S(fp)
IF cc_ne,r1,0
 PUTC '0'
ENDIF
ELSE
 add r0,48
 PUTC
 lc r0,1
 sw r0,PD_S(fp)
ENDIF
 lw r0,PD_P(fp)
 add r0,3
 sw r0,PD_P(fp)
ENDDO
 mov r0,r2
 add r0,48
 PUTC
 RET
 .data

 .word 1000000,100000,10000,1000,100,10,1
 .text
ENDIFASM

; _svc_puthex(n): write n in lower-case hex, no leading zeros.
IFDEF NEED_svc_puthex
_svc_puthex:
 LOCAL PH_I,3
 LOCAL PH_S,3
 PROLOG
 ARG r2,1
 lc r0,0
 sw r0,PH_S(fp)
 lc r0,20
 sw r0,PH_I(fp)
DO
 mov r0,r2
 lw r1,PH_I(fp)
 srl r0,r1
 lc r1,15
 and r0,r1
; print from the first non-zero digit, and always the last one
IF cc_ne,r0,0
 lc r1,1
 sw r1,PH_S(fp)
ENDIF
 lw r1,PH_I(fp)
IF cc_eq,r1,0
 lc r1,1
 sw r1,PH_S(fp)
ENDIF
 lw r1,PH_S(fp)
IF cc_ne,r1,0
IF cc_lt,r0,10
 add r0,48
ELSE
 add r0,87
ENDIF
 PUTC
ENDIF
 lw r0,PH_I(fp)
 DOEXIT cc_eq,r0,0
 add r0,-4
 sw r0,PH_I(fp)
ENDDO
 RET
ENDIFASM

; to a whole number of words (as tc24r's malloc); returns the address.
IFDEF NEED_svc_getmain
IFNDEF SVC_HEAP
SVC_HEAP EQU 524288
ENDIFASM
_svc_getmain:
 PROLOG
 ARG r2,1
IF cc_lt,r2,3
 lc r2,3
ENDIF
 mov r1,r2
DO
 DOEXIT cc_lt,r1,3
 add r1,-3
ENDDO
IF cc_ne,r1,0
 sub r2,r1
 add r2,3
ENDIF
 la r1,_svc_heap_ptr
 lw r0,0(r1)
 add r2,r0
 sw r2,0(r1)
 RET
 .data

 .word SVC_HEAP
 .text
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM

; lib/check.hlasm -- the tiny-C demos' self-test pattern (macros only):
;   CHECKINIT                  ok = 1
;   CHECK cc_eq,r0,25          ok = 0 unless r0 = 25   (C: if (x != 25) ok = 0;)
;   CHECKEND "D13OK\n",42      if ok: write the text, r0 = 42; else r0 = 0
; Needs: frame, svc_bare. The flag lives in one word, _chk_ok, defined by
; CHECKINIT (so use CHECKINIT once per program). Each macro clobbers r0
; and r1; CHECK leaves its operands alone.
IFNDEF LIB_CHECK
SET LIB_CHECK,1

MACRO CHECKINIT
 .data
_chk_ok:
 .word 0
 .text
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lc r0,1
 sw r0,0(r1)
MEND

; CHECK cond,a,b -- a structured condition (any cc_ form, a register and a
; register or value); when it is false the ok flag is cleared.
MACRO CHECK &C,&A,&B
IF &C,&A,&B
ELSE
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lc r0,0
 sw r0,0(r1)
ENDIF
MEND

; CHECKEND "text",rc -- if every CHECK held, write text and set r0 = rc
; (a register, constant or label); otherwise r0 = 0.
MACRO CHECKEND &T,&RC
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lw r0,0(r1)
IF cc_ne,r0,0
 WTO &T
 LOADR r0,&RC
ELSE
 lc r0,0
ENDIF
MEND
ENDIFASM

# The hlasm macro library: one COPY member per file. A program's sourceset

#   SOURCESET <path to>/lib/lib.sourceset
# and the program COPYs the members it needs: macro members at the top,
# the code members (svc_bare_code, rt_code) at the end.

COPY svc_bare svc_bare.hlasm
COPY svc_bare_code svc_bare_code.hlasm

EOF

; Library test: console output (PUTC, PUTNL, PUTS, WTO, PUTDEC, PUTHEX),
; START and the r0 report, STR. Prints:
;   AB
;   hi there
;   0 7 -1 42 1000000 8388607 -8388608
;   0 ff abc ffffff
;   r0=5
COPY cor24
COPY frame
COPY svc_bare
COPY data
SET SHOWRC,1
 START
_main:
 PROLOG
 PUTC 'A'
 lc r2,66

 PUTNL
 STR msg,"hi"

 PUTDEC 0

 lc r0,-1
 PUTDEC
 PUTC ' '
 PUTDEC 42

 PUTDEC 1000000
 PUTC ' '
 PUTDEC 8388607
 PUTC ' '
 la r2,8388608
 PUTDEC r2
 PUTNL

 PUTHEX 255
 PUTC ' '
 PUTHEX 2748
 PUTC ' '
 lc r0,-1
 PUTHEX r0
 PUTNL

COPY svc_bare_code
EOF

 LOCAL GL_N,3

 ARG r2,1
 lc r0,0

DO

 ARG r1,2

; lib/svc_bare.hlasm -- system services interface, bare-metal target
; (macros only). The routines these macros call are in svc_bare_code, which
; the program COPYs at its end; a routine is emitted only if a macro here
; asked for it (SET NEED_<name>,1). A sw-tos target can provide the same
; macros on top of IPC without changing the programs.
; Needs: cor24, frame.
;
; Register effects: every macro may clobber r0 and r1 and preserves r2 and
; fp, unless its description says otherwise.
IFNDEF LIB_SVC
SET LIB_SVC,1

; START [main] -- program entry: .text, _start calls main (default _main),
; then falls into _exit. Put it before any other code.
MACRO START &M=_main
 .text
_start:
 la r0,&M
 jal r1,(r0)
 EXITCODE
MEND

; EXITCODE -- the program's exit path (used by START): _exit, then with
; SET SHOWRC,1 print "r0=<n>" and a newline (n is r0, the exit code),
; then halt (bra to itself, which cor24-emu treats as a stop).
MACRO EXITCODE
_exit:
IFDEF SHOWRC
 push r0
 lc r0,114
 PUTC
 lc r0,48
 PUTC
 lc r0,61
 PUTC
 pop r0
 push r0
 PUTDEC
 PUTNL
 pop r0
ENDIFASM
_halt:
 bra _halt
MEND

; EXIT [code] -- stop the program from anywhere: r0 = code (register,
; constant or label; default: r0 as it is), then jump to _exit.
MACRO EXIT &C=r0
 LOADR r0,&C
 la r1,_exit
 jmp (r1)
MEND

; PUTC [char] -- write one character to the UART, waiting while the
; transmitter is busy. char is a register (default r0), a constant or a
; character such as 'A'. Inline; clobbers r0 and r1.
MACRO PUTC &C=r0
 LOADR r0,&C
 push r2
 la r2,UART_DATA
L\@:
 lb r1,1(r2)
 cls r1,z
 brt L\@
 sb r0,0(r2)
 pop r2
MEND

; PUTNL -- write a newline (10).
MACRO PUTNL
 PUTC 10
MEND

; PUTS str -- write the NUL-terminated string at str (a label or a register
; holding its address). No newline is added.
MACRO PUTS &S
SET NEED_svc_puts,1
 CALL _svc_puts,&S
MEND

; PUTDEC [reg] -- write a value in signed decimal (default r0); a
; register, constant or label.
MACRO PUTDEC &V=r0
SET NEED_svc_putdec,1
 CALL _svc_putdec,&V
MEND

; PUTHEX [reg] -- write a value in lower-case hex without leading zeros
; (as tc24r's printf %x).
MACRO PUTHEX &V=r0
SET NEED_svc_puthex,1
 CALL _svc_puthex,&V
MEND

; WTO "text" -- write a literal string. The text is stored out of line in
; .data (escapes such as \n are resolved by hlasm).
MACRO WTO &T
 .data
WTO\@:
 .ascii &T
 .byte 0
 .text
 PUTS WTO\@
MEND

; GETC [reg] -- wait for a character from the UART and return it in r0
; (and reg, if given and not r0).
MACRO GETC &R=r0
SET NEED_svc_getc,1
 CALL _svc_getc
IFDIFF &R,r0
 mov &R,r0
ENDIFASM
MEND

; GETLINE buf,len -- read UART characters into buf until a newline (not
; stored) or len-1 characters; buf is NUL-terminated. r0 = the length.
MACRO GETLINE &B,&L
SET NEED_svc_getline,1
 CALL _svc_getline,&B,&L
MEND

; GETMAIN reg,size -- allocate size bytes (rounded up to whole words) from
; the heap (a bump allocator starting at SVC_HEAP, 0x080000 unless the
; program defines it first); reg = the address. reg is r0 or r2.
MACRO GETMAIN &R,&N
SET NEED_svc_getmain,1
 CALL _svc_getmain,&N
IFDIFF &R,r0
 mov &R,r0
ENDIFASM
MEND

; FREEMAIN reg,size -- release storage. A bump allocator does not reclaim
; it (as tc24r's free), so this generates no code.
MACRO FREEMAIN &R,&N
MEND
ENDIFASM

# sw-cor24-hlasm -- HLASM-Inspired Macro-Assembler for COR24

An IBM HLASM-inspired macro-assembler for the COR24 24-bit RISC ISA,
written entirely in COR24 assembly. Reads HLASM-inspired structured
source and produces plain COR24 assembly output via UART.

Part of the [COR24 ecosystem](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project).

## Features

**How to use it: [docs/user-guide.md](docs/user-guide.md)** (setup, running,
every feature with examples, limits and error messages).

- Named constants and expressions: `EQU`, `SET`, `* / % << >> & | ^ ~ ( )`,
  character literals; values are substituted into instruction and data
  operands (cor24-asm has no EQU)
- Macros with named, positional, default and keyword parameters and `\@`
  local labels; macros can call macros (8 deep, recursion allowed), and
  bodies can use conditional assembly, structured statements and
  `&SYSNARG` (argument count)
- Conditional assembly: `IFDEF`, `IFNDEF`, `IFEQ`, `IFNE`, `ELSEASM`
- Structured control flow: IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF, DO/DOEXIT/ITERATE/ENDDO,
  SELECT/WHEN/OTHERWISE/ENDSEL, with automatic long-range jumps
- Data conveniences: `.ascii`, `.asciz` (with `\xNN` escapes), `.space`,
  `.fill`
- Multi-file sources: `INCLUDE` / `COPY` members through source sets (32
  members, 15-character names, nesting 16)
- Optional annotations, listing, cross-reference and diagnostics
- Plain assembly passthrough; checked limits that stop with `ERROR:`
- Errors name the member and line: `ERROR: <member>:<line>: <message>`
- Planned: compound conditions, DSECT (see docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md)

## Opt-in Source Switches

All four are off by default and activated by a `SET <name>,1` line anywhere in the source:

- `SET HLANN,1` -- annotate structured control-flow lowering with `; HLASM ...` comments
- `SET HLIST,1` -- emit listing comments for COPY members, macro definitions, macro expansions, and selected consumed directives
- `SET HLXREF,1` -- emit a compact end-of-run cross-reference section
- `SET HLDIAG,1` -- activate the diagnostic channel (`; !! hlasm: <msg> at src<id>:<line>`)

## Pipeline

```
.hlasm source (in memory)
     |
     v
hlasm.s (macro-assembler running on COR24)
     |
     v
UART output: plain .s assembly
     |
     v
cor24-asm out.s -o out.lgo; cor24-emu --lgo out.lgo
```

## Prerequisites

- `cor24-asm` -- build from [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler)
- `cor24-emu` -- build from [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator)
  (`scripts/run-kernel.sh` finds both on PATH, via `COR24_ASM` / `COR24_EMU`,
  or in sibling checkouts' `target/release`)
- `reg-rs` -- for running tests

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build / assemble check
just build

# Run demo
just demo

# Run tests
just test

# Run the split bootstrap proof
just bootstrap

# Or use shell scripts directly:
./build.sh          # build / test / run
./demo.sh           # demo / test / repl
```

## Project Structure

```
hlasm.s        -- COR24 assembly source (the macro-assembler)
bootstrap/     -- reduced self-hosting subset sources and proof points
build.sh       -- build / test / run script
scripts/       -- run-kernel.sh: assemble a .s (cor24-asm) and run it (cor24-emu);
                  hlasm-e2e.sh: .hlasm -> hlasm -> cor24-asm -> cor24-emu, prints UART output
demo.sh        -- demo script
justfile       -- just targets
docs/          -- architecture, prd, design, plan
reg-rs/        -- reg-rs test specifications and baselines
```

## Documentation

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) -- system overview and memory layout
- [Bootstrap Plan](docs/bootstrap.md) -- staged self-hosting path and blockers
- [PRD](docs/prd.md) -- product requirements and scope
- [Design](docs/design.md) -- syntax, lowering rules, data structures
- [Plan](docs/plan.md) -- step-by-step implementation roadmap

## Related Repositories

- [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator) -- COR24 emulator (`cor24-emu`)
- [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler) -- COR24 cross-assembler (`cor24-asm`)
- [sw-cor24-forth](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-forth) -- Forth for COR24
- [sw-cor24-rpg-ii](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-rpg-ii) -- RPG-II for COR24
- [sw-cor24-project](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project) -- ecosystem hub

# sw-cor24-hlasm -- HLASM-Inspired Macro-Assembler for COR24

An IBM HLASM-inspired macro-assembler for the COR24 24-bit RISC ISA,
written entirely in COR24 assembly. Reads HLASM-inspired structured
source and produces plain COR24 assembly output via UART.

Part of the [COR24 ecosystem](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project).

## Features

**How to use it: [docs/user-guide.md](docs/user-guide.md)** (setup, running,
every feature with examples, limits and error messages).

- Named constants and expressions: `EQU`, `SET`, `* / % << >> & | ^ ~ ( )`,
  character literals; values are substituted into instruction and data
  operands (cor24-asm has no EQU)
- Macros with named, positional, default and keyword parameters and `\@`
  local labels; macros can call macros (8 deep, recursion allowed), and
  bodies can use conditional assembly, structured statements and
  `&SYSNARG` (argument count)
- Conditional assembly: `IFDEF`, `IFNDEF`, `IFEQ`, `IFNE`, `ELSEASM`
- Structured control flow: IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF, DO/DOEXIT/ITERATE/ENDDO,
  SELECT/WHEN/OTHERWISE/ENDSEL, with automatic long-range jumps
- Data conveniences: `.ascii`, `.asciz` (with `\xNN` escapes), `.space`,
  `.fill`
- Multi-file sources: `INCLUDE` / `COPY` members through source sets (32
  members, 15-character names, nesting 16)
- Optional annotations, listing, cross-reference and diagnostics
- Plain assembly passthrough; checked limits that stop with `ERROR:`
- Errors name the member and line: `ERROR: <member>:<line>: <message>`
- Planned: compound conditions, DSECT (see docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md)

## Opt-in Source Switches

All four are off by default and activated by a `SET <name>,1` line anywhere in the source:

- `SET HLANN,1` -- annotate structured control-flow lowering with `; HLASM ...` comments
- `SET HLIST,1` -- emit listing comments for COPY members, macro definitions, macro expansions, and selected consumed directives
- `SET HLXREF,1` -- emit a compact end-of-run cross-reference section
- `SET HLDIAG,1` -- activate the diagnostic channel (`; !! hlasm: <msg> at src<id>:<line>`)

## Pipeline

```
.hlasm source (in memory)
     |
     v
hlasm.s (macro-assembler running on COR24)
     |
     v
UART output: plain .s assembly
     |
     v
cor24-asm out.s -o out.lgo; cor24-emu --lgo out.lgo
```

## Prerequisites

- `cor24-asm` -- build from [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler)
- `cor24-emu` -- build from [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator)
  (`scripts/run-kernel.sh` finds both on PATH, via `COR24_ASM` / `COR24_EMU`,
  or in sibling checkouts' `target/release`)
- `reg-rs` -- for running tests

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build / assemble check
just build

# Run demo
just demo

# Run tests
just test

# Run the split bootstrap proof
just bootstrap

# Or use shell scripts directly:
./build.sh          # build / test / run
./demo.sh           # demo / test / repl
```

## Project Structure

```
hlasm.s        -- COR24 assembly source (the macro-assembler)
bootstrap/     -- reduced self-hosting subset sources and proof points
build.sh       -- build / test / run script
scripts/       -- run-kernel.sh: assemble a .s (cor24-asm) and run it (cor24-emu);
                  hlasm-e2e.sh: .hlasm -> hlasm -> cor24-asm -> cor24-emu, prints UART output
demo.sh        -- demo script
justfile       -- just targets
docs/          -- architecture, prd, design, plan
reg-rs/        -- reg-rs test specifications and baselines
```

## Documentation

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) -- system overview and memory layout
- [Bootstrap Plan](docs/bootstrap.md) -- staged self-hosting path and blockers
- [PRD](docs/prd.md) -- product requirements and scope
- [Design](docs/design.md) -- syntax, lowering rules, data structures
- [Plan](docs/plan.md) -- step-by-step implementation roadmap

## Related Repositories

- [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator) -- COR24 emulator (`cor24-emu`)
- [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler) -- COR24 cross-assembler (`cor24-asm`)
- [sw-cor24-forth](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-forth) -- Forth for COR24
- [sw-cor24-rpg-ii](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-rpg-ii) -- RPG-II for COR24
- [sw-cor24-project](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project) -- ecosystem hub

## Copyright

Copyright (c) 2026 Michael A. Wright

## License

MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the full text.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# sw-cor24-hlasm -- HLASM-Inspired Macro-Assembler for COR24

An IBM HLASM-inspired macro-assembler for the COR24 24-bit RISC ISA,
written entirely in COR24 assembly. Reads HLASM-inspired structured
source and produces plain COR24 assembly output via UART.

Part of the [COR24 ecosystem](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project).

## Features

**How to use it: [docs/user-guide.md](docs/user-guide.md)** (setup, running,
every feature with examples, limits and error messages).

- Named constants and expressions: `EQU`, `SET`, `* / % << >> & | ^ ~ ( )`,
  character literals; values are substituted into instruction and data
  operands (cor24-asm has no EQU)
- Macros with named, positional, default and keyword parameters and `\@`
  local labels; macros can call macros (8 deep, recursion allowed), and
  bodies can use conditional assembly, structured statements and
  `&SYSNARG` (argument count)
- Conditional assembly: `IFDEF`, `IFNDEF`, `IFEQ`, `IFNE`, `ELSEASM`, and
  `IFSAME`/`IFDIFF` text tests so a macro can tell a register argument from
  a constant or label
- Structured control flow: IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF, DO/DOEXIT/ITERATE/ENDDO,
  SELECT/WHEN/OTHERWISE/ENDSEL, with automatic long-range jumps; conditions
  `cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt`, `cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge` and unsigned
  `cc_lu`, `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`
- Data conveniences: `.ascii`, `.asciz` (with `\xNN` escapes), `.space`,
  `.fill`
- Multi-file sources: `INCLUDE` / `COPY` members through source sets (32
  members, 15-character names, nesting 16)
- Optional annotations, listing, cross-reference and diagnostics
- Plain assembly passthrough; checked limits that stop with `ERROR:`
- Errors name the member and line: `ERROR: <member>:<line>: <message>`
- One-command end-to-end runs: `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh prog.hlasm` (hlasm,
  then cor24-asm, then cor24-emu) prints the program's output

## Status

Done:

- All the features above, each with demos and regression tests
  (`./build.sh test`, 79 tests).
- Every limit in [docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md](docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md)
  that was scheduled has been lifted: 512 symbols, 256 macros, 64 KB of macro
  bodies, 32-deep nesting, 32 source members.
- Structured statements assemble at any branch distance
  ([docs/structured-jump-relaxation.md](docs/structured-jump-relaxation.md)).
- All prerequisites for writing hlasm in HLASM itself are met
  ([docs/bootstrap-hlasm.md](docs/bootstrap-hlasm.md)).

In progress: **porting the tiny-C demos to HLASM.** The example programs of
the tc24r C compiler (`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos`) are being rewritten in
HLASM on top of a shared macro library, to show what macros buy over plain
assembly. See [docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md](docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md) for the
ported demos and the macros used, and
[docs/tinyc-port-plan.md](docs/tinyc-port-plan.md) for the survey and the
port order. The survey and the hlasm features it called for are done; the
macro library is being written now, then the ports and a side-by-side
showcase.

Planned later: compound conditions (`AND`/`OR`), `DSECT` record layouts,
a sw-tos services target, and the hlasm-in-HLASM bootstrap.

; lib/data.hlasm -- labelled data (macros only). cor24-asm has no separate
; data section: data is placed exactly where the macro is called, so call
; these where execution never flows -- after a routine's RET, or in a block
; of data after the program's routines. No registers are changed.
IFNDEF LIB_DATA
SET LIB_DATA,1

; STR label,"text" -- a NUL-terminated string (escapes resolved by hlasm).
MACRO STR &L,&T
&L:
 .ascii &T
 .byte 0
MEND

; SPACE label,bytes -- bytes of zeroed storage.
MACRO SPACE &L,&N
&L:
 .space &N
MEND

; WORDS label,v1[,...,v8] -- one 24-bit word per value (constants, symbol
; expressions or labels).
MACRO WORDS &L,&V1,&V2,&V3,&V4,&V5,&V6,&V7,&V8
&L:
 DATAITEMS .word,&V1,&V2,&V3,&V4,&V5,&V6,&V7,&V8
MEND

; BYTES label,v1[,...,v8] -- one byte per value.
MACRO BYTES &L,&V1,&V2,&V3,&V4,&V5,&V6,&V7,&V8
&L:
 DATAITEMS .byte,&V1,&V2,&V3,&V4,&V5,&V6,&V7,&V8
MEND

; DATAITEMS directive,v1,...,v8 -- one directive line per value given
; (helper for WORDS and BYTES).
MACRO DATAITEMS &D,&V1,&V2,&V3,&V4,&V5,&V6,&V7,&V8
IFDIFF &V1,
 &D &V1
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V2,
 &D &V2
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V3,
 &D &V3
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V4,
 &D &V4
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V5,
 &D &V5
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V6,
 &D &V6
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V7,
 &D &V7
ENDIFASM
IFDIFF &V8,
 &D &V8
ENDIFASM
MEND
ENDIFASM

; lib/data.hlasm -- labelled data (macros only). cor24-asm has no separate
; data section: data is placed exactly where the macro is called, so call
; these where execution never flows -- after a routine's RET, or in a block
; of data after the program's routines. No registers are changed.
IFNDEF LIB_DATA
SET LIB_DATA,1

; STR label,"text" -- a NUL-terminated string (escapes resolved by hlasm).
MACRO STR &L,&T
&L:

; lib/check.hlasm -- the tiny-C demos' self-test pattern (macros only):
;   CHECKINIT                  ok = 1
;   CHECK cc_eq,r0,25          ok = 0 unless r0 = 25   (C: if (x != 25) ok = 0;)

; Needs: frame, svc_bare. The flag lives in one word, _chk_ok, defined by
; CHECKINIT (so use CHECKINIT once per program). Each macro clobbers r0
; and r1; CHECK leaves its operands alone.
IFNDEF LIB_CHECK
SET LIB_CHECK,1

MACRO CHECKINIT
 .data
_chk_ok:
 .word 0
 .text
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lc r0,1
 sw r0,0(r1)
MEND

; CHECK cond,a,b -- a structured condition (any cc_ form, a register and a
; register or value); when it is false the ok flag is cleared.
MACRO CHECK &C,&A,&B
IF &C,&A,&B
ELSE
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lc r0,0
 sw r0,0(r1)
ENDIF
MEND

; CHECKEND "text",rc -- if every CHECK held, write text and set r0 = rc
; (a register, constant or label); otherwise r0 = 0.
MACRO CHECKEND &T,&RC
 la r1,_chk_ok
 lw r0,0(r1)
IF cc_ne,r0,0
 WTO &T
 LOADR r0,&RC
ELSE
 lc r0,0
ENDIF
MEND
ENDIFASM

# sw-cor24-hlasm -- HLASM-Inspired Macro-Assembler for COR24

An IBM HLASM-inspired macro-assembler for the COR24 24-bit RISC ISA,
written entirely in COR24 assembly. Reads HLASM-inspired structured
source and produces plain COR24 assembly output via UART.

Part of the [COR24 ecosystem](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project).

## Features

**How to use it: [docs/user-guide.md](docs/user-guide.md)** (setup, running,
every feature with examples, limits and error messages).

- Named constants and expressions: `EQU`, `SET`, `* / % << >> & | ^ ~ ( )`,
  character literals; values are substituted into instruction and data
  operands (cor24-asm has no EQU)
- Macros with named, positional, default and keyword parameters and `\@`
  local labels; macros can call macros (8 deep, recursion allowed), and
  bodies can use conditional assembly, structured statements and
  `&SYSNARG` (argument count)
- Conditional assembly: `IFDEF`, `IFNDEF`, `IFEQ`, `IFNE`, `ELSEASM`, and
  `IFSAME`/`IFDIFF` text tests so a macro can tell a register argument from
  a constant or label
- Structured control flow: IF/ELSEIF/ELSE/ENDIF, DO/DOEXIT/ITERATE/ENDDO,
  SELECT/WHEN/OTHERWISE/ENDSEL, with automatic long-range jumps; conditions
  `cc_eq`, `cc_ne`, `cc_lt`, `cc_le`, `cc_gt`, `cc_ge` and unsigned
  `cc_lu`, `cc_leu`, `cc_gtu`, `cc_geu`
- Data conveniences: `.ascii`, `.asciz` (with `\xNN` escapes), `.space`,
  `.fill`
- Multi-file sources: `INCLUDE` / `COPY` members through source sets (32
  members, 15-character names, nesting 16)
- Optional annotations, listing, cross-reference and diagnostics
- Plain assembly passthrough; checked limits that stop with `ERROR:`
- Errors name the member and line: `ERROR: <member>:<line>: <message>`
- One-command end-to-end runs: `scripts/hlasm-e2e.sh prog.hlasm` (hlasm,
  then cor24-asm, then cor24-emu) prints the program's output

## Status

Done:

- All the features above, each with demos and regression tests
  (`./build.sh test`, 79 tests).
- Every limit in [docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md](docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md)
  that was scheduled has been lifted: 512 symbols, 256 macros, 64 KB of macro
  bodies, 32-deep nesting, 32 source members.
- Structured statements assemble at any branch distance
  ([docs/structured-jump-relaxation.md](docs/structured-jump-relaxation.md)).
- All prerequisites for writing hlasm in HLASM itself are met
  ([docs/bootstrap-hlasm.md](docs/bootstrap-hlasm.md)).

In progress: **porting the tiny-C demos to HLASM.** The example programs of
the tc24r C compiler (`../sw-cor24-x-tinyc/demos`) are being rewritten in
HLASM on top of a shared macro library, to show what macros buy over plain
assembly. See [docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md](docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md) for the
ported demos and the macros used, and
[docs/tinyc-port-plan.md](docs/tinyc-port-plan.md) for the survey and the
port order. The survey and the hlasm features it called for are done; the
macro library is being written now, then the ports and a side-by-side
showcase.

Planned later: compound conditions (`AND`/`OR`), `DSECT` record layouts,
a sw-tos services target, and the hlasm-in-HLASM bootstrap.

## Opt-in Source Switches

All four are off by default and activated by a `SET <name>,1` line anywhere in the source:

- `SET HLANN,1` -- annotate structured control-flow lowering with `; HLASM ...` comments
- `SET HLIST,1` -- emit listing comments for COPY members, macro definitions, macro expansions, and selected consumed directives
- `SET HLXREF,1` -- emit a compact end-of-run cross-reference section
- `SET HLDIAG,1` -- activate the diagnostic channel (`; !! hlasm: <msg> at src<id>:<line>`)

## Pipeline

```
.hlasm source (in memory)
     |
     v
hlasm.s (macro-assembler running on COR24)
     |
     v
UART output: plain .s assembly
     |
     v
cor24-asm out.s -o out.lgo; cor24-emu --lgo out.lgo
```

## Prerequisites

- `cor24-asm` -- build from [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler)
- `cor24-emu` -- build from [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator)
  (`scripts/run-kernel.sh` finds both on PATH, via `COR24_ASM` / `COR24_EMU`,
  or in sibling checkouts' `target/release`)
- `reg-rs` -- for running tests

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build / assemble check
just build

# Run demo
just demo

# Run tests
just test

# Run the split bootstrap proof
just bootstrap

# Or use shell scripts directly:
./build.sh          # build / test / run
./demo.sh           # demo / test / repl
```

## Project Structure

```
hlasm.s        -- COR24 assembly source (the macro-assembler)
bootstrap/     -- reduced self-hosting subset sources and proof points
build.sh       -- build / test / run script
scripts/       -- run-kernel.sh: assemble a .s (cor24-asm) and run it (cor24-emu);
                  hlasm-e2e.sh: .hlasm -> hlasm -> cor24-asm -> cor24-emu, prints UART output
demo.sh        -- demo script
demos/         -- demo programs (d01-d43) and their source sets
justfile       -- just targets
docs/          -- user guide, architecture, plans
reg-rs/        -- reg-rs test specifications and baselines
```

## Documentation

- [User Guide](docs/user-guide.md) -- setup, running, every feature, limits
- [C Demos in HLASM](docs/c-demos-in-hlasm.md) -- the tiny-C example programs
  ported to HLASM, and the macro library they use
- [Tiny-C Port Plan](docs/tinyc-port-plan.md) -- survey of the C demos, macro
  catalog, port order, feature gaps
- [Limits and Lifting Plan](docs/limits-and-lifting-plan.md) -- every limit,
  defect and language gap, and when each was fixed
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) -- system overview and memory layout
- [Bootstrap Plan](docs/bootstrap.md) -- staged self-hosting path and blockers
- [hlasm in HLASM](docs/bootstrap-hlasm.md) -- plan for rewriting hlasm in its
  own language
- [PRD](docs/prd.md) -- product requirements and scope
- [Design](docs/design.md) -- syntax, lowering rules, data structures
- [Plan](docs/plan.md) -- the original (phase 1) implementation roadmap

## Related Repositories

- [sw-cor24-emulator](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-emulator) -- COR24 emulator (`cor24-emu`)
- [sw-cor24-x-assembler](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-x-assembler) -- COR24 cross-assembler (`cor24-asm`)
- [sw-cor24-forth](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-forth) -- Forth for COR24
- [sw-cor24-rpg-ii](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-rpg-ii) -- RPG-II for COR24
- [sw-cor24-project](https://github.com/sw-embed/sw-cor24-project) -- ecosystem hub

; lib/frame.hlasm -- routine frames and calls (macros only, no code).
;
; The calling convention is tc24r's, so these routines and tc24r-compiled
; ones can call each other:
;   caller: push the arguments right to left (one word each), jal, and pop
;           them; the result comes back in r0
;   callee: push fp, r2, r1; mov fp,sp; locals below fp; the first argument
;           is at 9(fp), the second at 12(fp), ...
; r0 and r1 are scratch across a call; r2 and fp are preserved.
;
; A routine looks like this:
;   _sum3:
;    LOCAL TMP,3          ; optional: name a 3-byte local (TMP = -3)
;    PROLOG               ; frame; reserves the LOCAL bytes
;    ARG r0,1             ; r0 = first argument
;    ARG r1,2
;    add r0,r1
;    sw r0,TMP(fp)
;    ...
;    RET                  ; result in r0
IFNDEF LIB_FRAME
SET LIB_FRAME,1
; bytes of LOCALs declared since the last PROLOG
SET LOCSZ,0

; LOADR reg,value -- reg = value, where value is a register (mov, or nothing
; if it is reg itself), or a constant, character or label (la).
MACRO LOADR &R,&V
IFDIFF &R,&V
IFSAME &V,r0
 mov &R,r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &V,r1
 mov &R,r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &V,r2
 mov &R,r2
ELSEASM
 la &R,&V
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND

; PUSHARG value -- push one call argument: a register as it is; a constant,
; character or label through r1 (so r1 is clobbered).
MACRO PUSHARG &A
IFSAME &A,r0
 push r0
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r1
 push r1
ELSEASM
IFSAME &A,r2
 push r2
ELSEASM
 la r1,&A
 push r1
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
ENDIFASM
MEND

; CALL fn[,a1,...,a8] -- call fn with up to 8 arguments, pushed right to left

;
; The calling convention is tc24r's, so these routines and tc24r-compiled
; ones can call each other:
;   caller: push the arguments right to left (one word each), jal, and pop
;           them; the result comes back in r0
;   callee: push fp, r2, r1; mov fp,sp; locals below fp; the first argument
;           is at 9(fp), the second at 12(fp), ...
; r0 and r1 are scratch across a call; r2 and fp are preserved.
;
; A routine looks like this:
;   _sum3:
;    LOCAL TMP,3          ; optional: name a 3-byte local (TMP = -3)
;    PROLOG               ; frame; reserves the LOCAL bytes
;    ARG r0,1             ; r0 = first argument
;    ARG r1,2
;    add r0,r1
;    sw r0,TMP(fp)
;    ...

SET LIB_FRAME,1
; bytes of LOCALs declared since the last PROLOG
SET LOCSZ,0

IFDIFF &R,&V
IFSAME &V,r0

ELSEASM
